The literal: value passes the required-field check and allows the parse to proceed. The detail enrichment stage overwrites it with the real extracted date.

Important: A literal: startTime is a bootstrap aid, not a contributor handoff value. Confirm that detail enrichment is running and that validation.sampleEvents show real extracted dates — not 2026-01-01 — before marking the schema ready.

docs.title: Event Identity
docs.text: Stable external IDs are required for reliable deduplication and update behavior.

docs.title: Priority Order
docs.text:
1. explicit event ID attribute
  2. event detail page URL
  3. slug or permalink
  4. generated fallback

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Good: - id: a::attr(href)

Acceptable: - id: xpath=.//a/@href

Avoid: - ID derived from visible title text alone

docs.title: Field Behavior
docs.text: External ID fallback order at runtime: 1. mappings.id 2. resolved event URL 3. generated fallback ID

docs.title: HtmlLite Source Submission Overview
docs.text:
Use HtmlLite when onboarding a new source that serves static HTML containing event cards.

For a machine-readable authoring contract, use the contributor-facing HtmlLite JSON Schema.

If you are not sure the source should use HtmlLite, start with Choose A Source Type before building selectors.

This reference is shared by both tracks: - human source contributor workflow - autonomous AI source onboarding workflow

docs.title: HtmlLite Quick Reference
docs.text:
• eventCardSelector: selector for repeating event nodes
  • mappings values: strings only
  • Text extraction: selector
  • Attribute extraction: selector@attribute or selector::attr(attribute)
  • Constant value: literal:...
  • Selector language: limited CSS-like selectors plus xpath=
  • detailPage.linkSelector must resolve to a URL
  • detailPage.detailMappings run against detail-page DOM
  • multiDateExpansion can fan out one card into multiple occurrences from a single date-list field
  • fieldTransforms supports deterministic low-risk per-field cleanup after extraction
  • deterministic extraction from canonical values such as query parameters is allowed when the source field already contains stable machine-readable data
  • Detail-page enrichment runs when both detailPage.enabled=true and WHENEBER_HTMLLITE_DETAIL_ENRICHMENT_ENABLED is not set to disable it
  • pagination.type allowed values: nextLink, queryIncrement, pathIncrement, fixedUrls
  • schemaDefinition must be sent as a JSON string in API payloads

v3 pipeline.calendar.type for HtmlLite

When building a v3 schemaDefinition for an HtmlLite source, set pipeline.calendar.type to "Html" — not "HtmlLite". The top-level source type field in the submission envelope remains "HtmlLite". See v3 Pipeline Examples.

Low-risk fieldTransforms types: - trim - collapseWhitespace - removePrefix - removeSuffix - replaceLiteral - stripWrappingQuotes - nullIfEqualsAny

Avoid high-risk transform patterns such as open-ended expression execution, brittle cross-field semantic reconstruction, or regex chains that guess at human-readable prose.

docs.title: Deterministic URL-Query Extraction Is Allowed
docs.text:
Some HtmlLite sources expose the most reliable datetime in a canonical attribute or URL query parameter rather than visible text. In those cases, deterministic extraction is allowed and is often preferable to parsing teaser text from the card.

Good fit: - a detail or export link contains machine-readable timestamps such as dates=20260409T020000Z/20260409T040000Z - the extraction can be described with one stable mapping and a short bounded transform chain - the transformed value is still derived from a single source field rather than reconstructed from unrelated fields

Bad fit: - the regex has to infer missing month, year, or meridiem from surrounding prose - the transform depends on card-specific wording or layout text - multiple unrelated fields must be merged to guess the final datetime

Use this pattern sparingly and document why the query value is the canonical source of truth.

See also: - Time Handling - Platform Patterns - Squarespace-Specific Patterns - Wix-Specific Selector Patterns

docs.title: Multi-Date Expansion
docs.text: Use multiDateExpansion when one event card contains a list of occurrence dates (for example theater showings).

docs.title: Contract summary
docs.text:
• multiDateExpansion.enabled: opt-in flag (default off)
  • multiDateExpansion.sourceField: mapped field containing the date-list text (usually startTime)
  • multiDateExpansion.limits: required bounds for per-card and per-run expansion
  • multiDateExpansion.fallbackMode: legacySingle or skipCard

docs.title: Precedence when combined with detailPage occurrence matching
docs.text:
HtmlLite supports composition with a strict precedence rule:

  1. multiDateExpansion determines event count (fan-out ownership)
  2. detailPage.occurrenceSelector only refines already-expanded events
  3. Detail occurrence matching cannot create or remove events

This avoids overlapping ownership and keeps output deterministic.

docs.title: Authoring note
docs.text: If your source currently uses a first-date-only regex workaround, prefer multiDateExpansion for true one-occurrence-per-performance output.

docs.title: AI-First Workflow From A Starting URL
docs.text:
Use this deterministic order to avoid 0-event failures:

  1. Find one stable repeating card selector.
  2. Map only title, url, and a parseable startTime first.
  3. Validate with POST /api/source-schemas/test-fetch.
  4. Add id and pagination.
  5. Add detailPage enrichment for time/location/description/image if list fields are incomplete.
  6. Re-validate after each change.

When detail mappings are configured but no enrichment is visible in parsed samples, verify the runtime flag WHENEBER_HTMLLITE_DETAIL_ENRICHMENT_ENABLED is enabled in the target environment.

If list-page time is unreliable, use a temporary parseable literal: start time to keep cards from being dropped, then overwrite with detail-page startDate + startTime mappings.

docs.title: Human Workflow Variant
docs.text: Use the same order as AI-first workflow, but validate after each manual selector change and keep notes on: - why each selector was chosen - what failed and how it was corrected - final validation evidence for admin handoff

docs.title: Reliability Principles
docs.text:
• Parse success is necessary but not sufficient. Validate field completeness for product-facing fields.
  • Prefer schema-first fixes over runtime code changes.
  • Runtime/platform code changes are acceptable only when generic and reusable across all sources.
  • If list cards are teaser-only, use detail-page enrichment instead of brittle list selectors.
  • For API-backed sources, verify field projection is not suppressing rich fields such as long descriptions or address fields.

docs.title: End-to-End Flow
docs.text:
1. Confirm source compatibility with static HTML parsing.
  2. Build a minimal schema.
  3. Add identity, pagination, and detail-page rules.
  4. Test fetch, then submit Draft and review backend validation result.
  5. Handoff schema ID and validation notes for admin review.

docs.title: Endpoint Summary
docs.text:
• POST /api/source-schemas/test-fetch
  • POST /api/source-schemas/community-submissions

docs.title: Request Contract Rule
docs.text: schemaDefinition must be sent as a JSON string in request payloads.

docs.title: Submit Validation Result
docs.text:
The submit endpoint performs server-side fetch/parse validation and returns: - sourceSchema: the created Draft source schema - validation.isSuccess: pass/fail - validation.totalEventsParsed: parsed event count - validation.sampleEvents: sample parsed rows (up to 5) - validation.errorMessage: failure reason when validation fails

Quick interpretation: - Success: validation.isSuccess = true and validation.totalEventsParsed > 0 - Failure: validation.isSuccess = false and validation.errorMessage explains what to fix

See also: - API Workflow - Schema Basics - Validation Checklist - Troubleshooting

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text: Many sources span multiple pages.

docs.title: Compatibility Check
docs.text: Look for patterns such as: - ?page= - ?p= - /page/ - offset=

docs.title: Supported Modes
docs.text:
• nextLink with nextPageSelector
  • queryIncrement with parameter, start, step
  • pathIncrement with pathTemplate, start, step
  • fixedUrls with urls
  • maxPages for safety bounds

docs.title: Recommended Defaults
docs.text:
• start with nextLink when a reliable next-page element exists
  • use queryIncrement or pathIncrement when URLs are predictable and no next link exists
  • use fixedUrls for irregular page sets

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "pagination": {
    "type": "queryIncrement",
    "parameter": "page",
    "start": 0,
    "step": 1,
    "maxPages": 10
  }
}

docs.title: HtmlLite Platform Patterns
docs.text:
Use this page when the source is built on a well-known site builder or CMS that tends to produce repeatable DOM and link patterns.

Platform pages are intended to reduce repeated trial-and-error for common sources while keeping the core HtmlLite guidance generic.

docs.title: When To Use This Page
docs.text:
Use the platform-specific pages when: - the site clearly matches a known builder such as Squarespace or Wix - repeated onboarding work has shown stable extraction patterns for that platform - you need recognition guidance before choosing selectors or source type details

Do not use platform pages as a substitute for source-type selection. Start with Choose A Source Type if you have not yet confirmed that HtmlLite is the right choice.

docs.title: Platform Page Structure
docs.text: Each platform page should cover the same topics: - when to use the page - platform signatures and how to recognize it - recommended source type by scenario - common extraction patterns - datetime pitfalls and preferred source-of-truth fields - anti-patterns to avoid - validation checklist - troubleshooting and fallbacks - minimal working example - AI runbook guidance when an agent is performing the onboarding

docs.title: Available Platform Pages
docs.text:
• Squarespace-Specific Patterns
  • Wix-Specific Selector Patterns

docs.title: Suggested Next Candidates
docs.text: Add new platform pages only after repeated onboarding work shows a reusable pattern. Current likely candidates: - WordPress event plugins - Eventbrite-hosted or embedded event pages

docs.title: Shared Rules Across Platforms
docs.text:
• Prefer structured feeds over HtmlLite when a real ICS, RSS, or JSON source exists.
  • Prefer canonical machine-readable fields over visible marketing copy.
  • Keep transforms deterministic and bounded.
  • Validate against parsed samples, not just selector matches.
  • Document platform-specific assumptions in handoff notes when they affect long-term maintenance.

docs.title: Minimal Required Fields
docs.text:
• eventCardSelector
  • mappings.title
  • mappings.startTime
  • validation.requiredFields includes title and startTime

docs.title: Supported Mapping Keys
docs.text: Key Description id Stable external ID for deduplication. If absent, falls back to url, then a random GUID. Always map this. title Event title startTime Event start datetime endTime Event end datetime. Defaults to startTime + 1 hour if absent. startDate Optional helper field for pages that split the calendar date from the visible time. When present, startTime may be a time-only value or a range like 10:30 AM - 11:30 AM. endDate Optional helper field used with endTime when the end date differs from the start date or the page exposes end date separately. description Event description location Location string venueName Venue name venueAddress Venue address url Event URL (resolved to absolute) imageUrl Image URL (resolved to absolute) recurrenceRule RFC-5545 RRULE string (e.g. FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=TH) or human-readable text (e.g. Recurring weekly on Thursday). If omitted, the event is stored as a single instance.

docs.title: Minimal Example
docs.text:
{
  "eventCardSelector": "div.event-teaser",
  "mappings": {
    "title": "h3",
    "startTime": "xpath=.//time[@datetime]::attr(datetime)",
    "url": "a::attr(href)"
  },
  "validation": {
    "requiredFields": ["title", "startTime"]
  }
}

docs.title: Minimal Progression (Recommended)
docs.text:
Start small and validate each step.

Important: - literal: time values are bootstrap aids, not final handoff values - replace or override them with real extracted times before final contributor handoff whenever possible - do not add fields that are not part of the HtmlLite contract

Step 1:

{
  "eventCardSelector": "h2.event__title",
  "mappings": {
    "title": "a",
    "url": "a@href",
    "startTime": "literal:2026-01-01T00:00:00-08:00"
  },
  "validation": {
    "requiredFields": ["title", "startTime", "url"]
  }
}

Step 2: add id, pagination, and detail-page mappings after Step 1 returns non-zero events.

docs.title: Field Transforms (Low Risk)
docs.text:
Use fieldTransforms for deterministic per-field string cleanup after extraction and before validation.

Supported transform types:

  • trim
  • collapseWhitespace
  • removePrefix
  • removeSuffix
  • replaceLiteral
  • stripWrappingQuotes
  • nullIfEqualsAny
  • regexReplace — matches a regex pattern and replaces it with a fixed string. Use value for the pattern, replacement for the substitution string, and ignoreCase to control case sensitivity. See Time Handling for worked examples.

Important:

  • Keep transforms simple and local to one field.
  • Prefer ReplaceLiteral for exact string cleanup — use RegexReplace only when a deterministic literal replace cannot isolate the target substring.
  • Apply RegexReplace as the first transform in the chain when stripping a trailing portion of a string (for example, removing a second performance date).

Example:

{
  "eventCardSelector": "div.event-card",
  "mappings": {
    "title": "h3",
    "startTime": "time::attr(datetime)",
    "location": ".event-location",
    "url": "a::attr(href)"
  },
  "fieldTransforms": {
    "location": [
      { "type": "removePrefix", "value": "Event location:", "ignoreCase": true },
      { "type": "stripWrappingQuotes" },
      { "type": "collapseWhitespace" },
      { "type": "trim" },
      { "type": "nullIfEqualsAny", "values": ["Online Meeting", "TBD"], "ignoreCase": true }
    ]
  },
  "validation": {
    "requiredFields": ["title", "startTime", "url"]
  }
}

docs.title: Do not add unsupported top-level fields
docs.text:
Invalid:

{
  "sourceName": "Example Events",
  "baseUrl": "https://example.org",
  "eventCardSelector": "div.event-card",
  "mappings": {
    "title": "h3",
    "startTime": ".date"
  }
}

Why invalid: - sourceName and baseUrl are not part of schemaDefinition

docs.title: Do not add top-level transforms
docs.text:
Invalid:

{
  "eventCardSelector": "div.event-card",
  "mappings": {
    "url": "a@href"
  },
  "transforms": [
    {
      "field": "url",
      "type": "absoluteUrl"
    }
  ]
}

Why invalid: - top-level transforms is not part of the HtmlLite schema - use fieldTransforms instead for safe per-field cleanup

docs.title: Use venueAddress, not address
docs.text:
Invalid:

{
  "detailPage": {
    "enabled": true,
    "detailMappings": {
      "address": ".event-address"
    }
  }
}

Valid:

{
  "detailPage": {
    "enabled": true,
    "detailMappings": {
      "venueAddress": ".event-address"
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Split Date And Time Is Usually Better Than Guessing
docs.text:
If a page shows date and time separately, prefer startDate plus startTime over guessing one combined selector.

Example:

{
  "eventCardSelector": "article.event",
  "mappings": {
    "id": "h2 a@href",
    "title": "h2 a",
    "startDate": ".event__date",
    "startTime": ".event__time",
    "url": "h2 a@href"
  },
  "validation": {
    "requiredFields": ["title", "startTime"]
  }
}

Do not map startTime to a date-only node and endTime to a time-only node unless you have proven that structure is valid for the page.

docs.title: Full Example
docs.text:
{
  "eventCardSelector": "div.event-teaser",
  "mappings": {
    "id": "a::attr(href)",
    "title": "h3",
    "startTime": "xpath=.//time[@datetime]::attr(datetime)",
    "description": ".event-teaser__description",
    "location": ".event-teaser__address",
    "venueName": "literal:My Venue",
    "venueAddress": ".event-teaser__address",
    "url": "a::attr(href)",
    "imageUrl": "img::attr(src)",
    "recurrenceRule": ".event-recurrence::attr(data-rrule)"
  },
  "detailPage": {
    "enabled": false
  },
  "pagination": {
    "type": "nextLink",
    "nextPageSelector": ".pager-next a::attr(href)",
    "maxPages": 10
  },
  "validation": {
    "requiredFields": ["title", "startTime"]
  }
}

docs.title: Split Date And Time Example
docs.text:
Use helper date mappings when the page exposes date and time in separate elements.

{
  "eventCardSelector": "article.event",
  "mappings": {
    "id": "h2 a@href",
    "title": "h2 a",
    "startDate": ".event__date",
    "startTime": ".event__time",
    "location": ".event__location",
    "url": "h2 a@href"
  },
  "validation": {
    "requiredFields": ["title", "startTime"]
  }
}

In this mode, HtmlLite combines startDate with startTime. If startTime contains a visible range such as 10:30 AM - 11:30 AM, the parser uses the first time for StartTime and the second time for EndTime.

docs.title: Known-Good Bootstrap Pattern (Multnomah Example)
docs.text:
Use this pattern for Drupal list pages where real time precision is on detail pages:

{
  "eventCardSelector": "h2.event__title",
  "mappings": {
    "id": "a@href",
    "title": "a",
    "url": "a@href",
    "startTime": "literal:2026-01-01T00:00:00-08:00"
  },
  "detailPage": {
    "enabled": true,
    "linkSelector": "a@href",
    "detailMappings": {
      "title": "h1",
      "url": "link[rel='canonical']@href",
      "startDate": ".event__date",
      "startTime": ".event__time",
      "location": ".event__location",
      "description": ".event__body",
      "imageUrl": ".field--name-field-event-image img@src"
    }
  },
  "pagination": {
    "type": "queryIncrement",
    "parameter": "page",
    "start": 0,
    "step": 1,
    "maxPages": 3
  },
  "validation": {
    "requiredFields": ["title", "startTime", "url"]
  }
}

This schema is a validated bootstrap pattern for non-zero event parsing on the Multnomah source.

docs.title: Discovery Workflow
docs.text:
1. Identify the repeating event card container.
  2. Map title, time, url first.
  3. Add description, location, image after submit validation succeeds.

Good card candidates: - div.views-row - li.event-card - article.event - div.event-teaser

docs.title: Supported Selector Patterns
docs.text:
• CSS-like selection:
  • tag, class, id, descendant by space
  • XPath:
  • prefix with xpath=
  • Attribute extraction:
  • selector::attr(name)
  • selector@attrName
  • Literal values:
  • literal:Some fixed value

Examples: - div.event-card - .event-title a - xpath=.//time[@datetime] - a::attr(href) - img@src

docs.title: Selector Scope Rules
docs.text:
• eventCardSelector runs against the listing page document.
  • mappings selectors run relative to each matched event card node.
  • detailPage.linkSelector runs relative to the matched event card node.
  • detailPage.detailMappings selectors run against the fetched detail page document.

Scope example:

  • If eventCardSelector is h2.event__title then mapping title: "a" selects the anchor inside that <h2>.
  • In detailMappings, title: "h1" selects from the detail page root, not the list page card.

docs.title: CSS-like vs XPath
docs.text:
HtmlLite is not XPath-only. It supports a limited CSS-like subset and raw XPath.

Use XPath when: - you need child combinators like > - you need selector lists like .a, .b - you need sibling logic, nth/first filters, or attribute predicates beyond the simple subset - you need conditional logic or explicit node tests

XPath examples: - xpath=.//time[@datetime] - xpath=.//img[1] - xpath=.//h2[@class='event-title']/a

XPath selectors with attribute predicates (for example [@class='...']) are supported.

Use CSS-like selectors when: - matching simple class/id/tag structures - using descendant-by-space selectors like h2 a - extracting direct attributes with ::attr(...)

CSS-like examples: - img::attr(src) - a::attr(href) - h2.event__title a

Avoid unsupported CSS syntax in HtmlLite:

  • > child combinator
  • selector lists separated by commas
  • pseudo-selectors like :first-child
  • adjacent and general sibling operators

If you need any of those, switch that selector to xpath= instead of trying to force full CSS syntax.

docs.title: CSS-to-XPath Quick Reference
docs.text:
Why CSS attribute selectors fail: HtmlLite converts selectors to XPath for DOM traversal. CSS attribute selectors like [id^="prefix"] produce invalid XPath syntax. Use starts-with() instead.

CSS Selector XPath When To Use [id^="prefix"] .//*[starts-with(@id, "prefix")] Match elements by ID prefix (Wix components, dynamic IDs) [class*="event"] .//*[contains(@class, "event")] Match elements by partial class name .class-name .//*[@class="class-name"] or .//*[contains(@class, "class-name")] Match by exact class or class presence element > child element/child Direct child only (one level down) element descendant element//descendant Any-depth descendant a[href$=".html"] a[ends-with(@href, ".html")] Attribute value ends with a[href*="search"] a[contains(@href, "search")] Attribute value contains

docs.title: Wix-Specific Selector Patterns
docs.text:
Wix pages do not all expose the same stable selector strategy.

Prefer this order: 1. semantic data-hook selectors on Wix Events pages 2. machine-readable attributes when available 3. repeatable comp-* component prefixes on Wix CMS repeater pages

Wix Events pages often expose server-rendered hooks such as events-card, title, date, and location:

{
  "eventCardSelector": "[data-hook='events-card']",
  "mappings": {
    "title": "a[data-hook='title']",
    "startTime": "[data-hook='date']",
    "location": "[data-hook='location']",
    "url": "a[data-hook='title']@href"
  }
}

When those hooks are missing, Wix CMS sites (built with Wix Editor) often use repeatable component ID patterns:

Repeater Items:

.//*[starts-with(@id, "comp-mcsmgbbs__")]   // Match any element with ID prefix
.//*[starts-with(@id, "comp-")]//h2         // Get h2 inside Wix component

Common Wix Component IDs: - comp-mcsmgbbs__ - Rich text / title elements - comp-mcsn738v__ - Date / schedule elements - comp-md8it4c0__ - Button / link elements - comp-mcsmgbbu1__ - Description / paragraph elements

Why prefixes work: Wix repeater components use stable ID prefixes (e.g., comp-mcsmgbbs__) that don't change between page reloads. The suffix (UUID) is unique per repeater item. Using starts-with() on the prefix reliably matches all event cards.

Fallback Wix CMS Schema:

{
  "eventCardSelector": ".wixui-repeater__item",
  "mappings": {
    "title": ".//*[starts-with(@id, \"comp-mcsmgbbs__\")]//h2",
    "startTime": ".//*[starts-with(@id, \"comp-mcsn738v__\")]//h4",
    "description": ".//*[starts-with(@id, \"comp-mcsmgbbu1__\")]//p",
    "url": ".//*[starts-with(@id, \"comp-md8it4c0__\")]//a/@href"
  }
}

For a fuller Wix decision tree and fallback guidance, see wix-specific-patterns.md.

Unsupported mapping syntax:

  • regex:(...) is not a supported selector or mapping DSL in HtmlLite

If a date/time value needs normalization beyond selector extraction:

  1. prefer extracting machine-readable attributes first (for example time::attr(datetime))
  2. use startDate plus startTime when the page splits date/time
  3. if the source requires heavy transformation, consider JsonApi instead of HtmlLite

docs.title: Invalid vs Valid Examples
docs.text:
Chat models often try to hedge with multiple fallback selectors in a single string. That does not work in HtmlLite.

Invalid:

{
  "eventCardSelector": ".event-listing, .events-listing-item, .event-item",
  "mappings": {
    "title": ".event-title, h3, h2"
  }
}

Why invalid: - selector lists separated by commas are unsupported

Valid:

{
  "eventCardSelector": "xpath=.//*[contains(@class,'event-listing') or contains(@class,'events-listing-item') or contains(@class,'event-item')]",
  "mappings": {
    "title": "xpath=.//*[contains(@class,'event-title') or self::h3 or self::h2][1]"
  }
}

Also avoid invented selectors that are not proven by the page source. A weaker but evidenced selector is better than a broader guessed one.

docs.title: Compound Class Selectors on WordPress and Page-Builder Sites
docs.text:
Some WordPress themes (including BeTheme with Muffin Builder, Divi, and similar builders) generate elements with multiple compound classes, for example <div class="mcb-wrap three-fifth">. Treating this as a CSS multi-class selector like div.mcb-wrap.three-fifth is not reliably supported in HtmlLite.

Use XPath contains(@class, '...') predicates instead:

"eventCardSelector": "xpath=.//div[contains(@class,'mcb-wrap') and contains(@class,'three-fifth')]"

To avoid matching non-event blocks on the page, add a child-presence guard — an inner predicate that requires a known child element to exist:

"eventCardSelector": "xpath=.//div[contains(@class,'mcb-wrap') and contains(@class,'three-fifth') and .//h2[@class='title']]"

This ensures only divs containing a title heading are matched as event cards.

docs.title: When To Use This Page
docs.text:
Use this page when the source is a Squarespace events listing and the initial HTML contains repeatable event cards.

This page is especially relevant when the visible card text splits date and time across separate nodes, but the card also includes a Google Calendar export link with canonical UTC timestamps.

docs.title: Platform Signatures
docs.text: Common Squarespace indicators: - page markup includes eventlist class names such as eventlist-event or eventlist-column-info - event cards are rendered in the initial HTML response - each card links to a detail page under a path like /events/<slug> - each card may expose a Google Calendar export URL containing a dates= query parameter

docs.title: Recommended Source Type By Scenario
docs.text:
• Use HtmlLite when the initial HTML already contains repeatable event cards.
  • Prefer Ics, Rss, or JsonApi if the platform exposes a real structured feed with event occurrence dates.
  • Do not choose Rss just because Squarespace exposes an RSS endpoint; validate that the feed contains actual event occurrence dates rather than publish dates.

docs.title: Card Selector
docs.text:
Typical repeating card selector:

"eventCardSelector": "article.eventlist-event.eventlist-event--upcoming"

docs.title: Basic Mappings
docs.text:
Typical card mappings:

{
  "mappings": {
    "title": ".eventlist-title-link",
    "url": ".eventlist-title-link@href",
    "eventUrl": ".eventlist-title-link@href",
    "description": ".eventlist-column-info",
    "imageUrl": ".eventlist-column-thumbnail img@src"
  }
}

docs.title: Canonical Datetime From Google Calendar Link
docs.text:
When the visible time text is incomplete or split, map the export link first and derive startTime and endTime from the dates= query value.

Example pattern:

{
  "mappings": {
    "startTime": ".eventlist-meta-export-google@href",
    "endTime": ".eventlist-meta-export-google@href"
  },
  "fieldTransforms": {
    "startTime": [
      { "type": "RegexReplace", "value": "^.*[?&]dates=([0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}Z)/([0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}Z).*$", "replacement": "$1" },
      { "type": "RegexReplace", "value": "^([0-9]{4})([0-9]{2})([0-9]{2})T([0-9]{2})([0-9]{2})([0-9]{2})Z$", "replacement": "$1-$2-$3T$4:$5:$6Z" }
    ],
    "endTime": [
      { "type": "RegexReplace", "value": "^.*[?&]dates=([0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}Z)/([0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}Z).*$", "replacement": "$2" },
      { "type": "RegexReplace", "value": "^([0-9]{4})([0-9]{2})([0-9]{2})T([0-9]{2})([0-9]{2})([0-9]{2})Z$", "replacement": "$1-$2-$3T$4:$5:$6Z" }
    ]
  }
}

Use this only when the export link is present consistently and the timestamps are clearly canonical.

docs.title: Datetime Pitfalls And Preferred Source Of Truth
docs.text:
Preferred extraction order for Squarespace events: 1. Google Calendar export URL timestamps 2. time[datetime] or structured datetime attributes 3. visible date/time text on the card

Common pitfalls: - RSS pubDate can reflect publish time rather than event occurrence time - visible card text may split month, day, and time into separate elements - list pages may omit end time even when the export link contains both timestamps

docs.title: Anti-Patterns To Avoid
docs.text:
• Do not reconstruct datetimes by stitching together unrelated marketing text fragments if the export link already provides the canonical timestamp.
  • Do not use a broad regex against the entire card HTML when a single href attribute is available.
  • Do not assume the Squarespace RSS feed is event-safe without checking real sample items.

docs.title: Validation Checklist
docs.text:
• verify validation.totalEventsParsed is close to the visible upcoming card count
  • confirm sampleEvents show the correct event occurrence date, not article publish date
  • confirm the exported URLs resolve to the same host or an expected detail host
  • confirm timezone assumptions match the venue locale when UTC timestamps are converted downstream

docs.title: Troubleshooting And Fallbacks
docs.text:
• If the Google export link is missing on some cards, fall back to time[datetime] or visible card time.
  • If the listing cards are teaser-only, keep the list-page schema minimal and use detail-page enrichment for description, venue, or image.
  • If the feed exposes paginated older events, add pagination only after the first page is parsing correctly.

docs.title: Minimal Working Example
docs.text:
{
  "eventCardSelector": "article.eventlist-event.eventlist-event--upcoming",
  "mappings": {
    "title": ".eventlist-title-link",
    "url": ".eventlist-title-link@href",
    "startTime": ".eventlist-meta-export-google@href",
    "endTime": ".eventlist-meta-export-google@href"
  },
  "fieldTransforms": {
    "startTime": [
      { "type": "RegexReplace", "value": "^.*[?&]dates=([0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}Z)/([0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}Z).*$", "replacement": "$1" },
      { "type": "RegexReplace", "value": "^([0-9]{4})([0-9]{2})([0-9]{2})T([0-9]{2})([0-9]{2})([0-9]{2})Z$", "replacement": "$1-$2-$3T$4:$5:$6Z" }
    ]
  },
  "validation": {
    "requiredFields": ["title", "startTime", "url"]
  }
}

docs.title: AI Runbook Notes
docs.text: When an AI agent is onboarding a Squarespace source: 1. Prove the cards exist in the initial HTML before committing to HtmlLite. 2. Probe RSS and ICS endpoints, but reject them if they do not carry event occurrence dates. 3. Check for export links on the card before attempting visible-text reconstruction. 4. Validate a minimal schema with title, url, and parseable startTime first. 5. Add endTime, detail-page enrichment, and pagination only after the initial parse is correct.

docs.title: Time Handling
docs.text: Time parsing is a common failure point.

docs.title: Preferred Extraction Order
docs.text:
1. time datetime attribute
  2. schema.org or meta startDate
  3. data-start or similar data attributes
  4. visible text parsing

Examples: - Preferred: xpath=.//time[@datetime]::attr(datetime) - Riskier: .event-time - Risky: visible text like 10:30 am - 11:30 am

docs.title: Canonical Datetime In A Link Or Query Parameter
docs.text:
Sometimes the visible card text is incomplete, but an export or detail link contains the canonical datetime in a stable query value.

This is an acceptable HtmlLite pattern when all of these are true: - the mapped field comes from one stable attribute such as an href - the query parameter is machine-readable and present consistently across cards - the transform chain is bounded and deterministic

Example: extract UTC start and end timestamps from a Google Calendar export link.

{
  "mappings": {
    "startTime": ".eventlist-meta-export-google@href",
    "endTime": ".eventlist-meta-export-google@href"
  },
  "fieldTransforms": {
    "startTime": [
      { "type": "RegexReplace", "value": "^.*[?&]dates=([0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}Z)/([0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}Z).*$", "replacement": "$1" },
      { "type": "RegexReplace", "value": "^([0-9]{4})([0-9]{2})([0-9]{2})T([0-9]{2})([0-9]{2})([0-9]{2})Z$", "replacement": "$1-$2-$3T$4:$5:$6Z" }
    ],
    "endTime": [
      { "type": "RegexReplace", "value": "^.*[?&]dates=([0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}Z)/([0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}Z).*$", "replacement": "$2" },
      { "type": "RegexReplace", "value": "^([0-9]{4})([0-9]{2})([0-9]{2})T([0-9]{2})([0-9]{2})([0-9]{2})Z$", "replacement": "$1-$2-$3T$4:$5:$6Z" }
    ]
  }
}

Prefer this over parsing teaser text when the link value is clearly the source of truth. Do not use it as a license for broad regex scraping against free-form copy.

docs.title: Split Date And Time Support
docs.text:
When the page separates date and time into different nodes, map:

  • startDate to the visible date node
  • startTime to either a time-only value or a visible range like 10:30 AM - 11:30 AM
  • optionally endDate and endTime if the end date is exposed separately

Example:

{
    "mappings": {
        "title": "h2 a",
        "startDate": ".event__date",
        "startTime": ".event__time",
        "url": "h2 a@href"
    }
}

Behavior:

  • If startTime is already a full datetime, HtmlLite uses it directly.
  • If startDate is present and startTime is time-only, HtmlLite combines them.
  • If startTime is a visible range like 10:30 AM - 11:30 AM, HtmlLite derives both StartTime and EndTime.
  • If no end can be derived, EndTime still defaults to StartTime + 1 hour.

For the v3 HTML calendar parser, recognizable yearless split dates use the current year when their month/day is today or later in the mapped event timezone, and next year otherwise. This compares dates, not event clock times. Explicit years remain unchanged, and invalid selected dates (including Feb 29 in a non-leap year) are skipped rather than replaced. This fallback can promote genuinely past events; prefer authoritative publisher years. See v3 yearless HTML semantics for details and the unchanged freshness policy.

docs.title: Validation Tips
docs.text:
• verify submit response validation.sampleEvents have parseable datetime values
  • verify timezone assumptions
  • verify AM/PM and all-day handling

docs.title: Date Range Parsing & Silent Failures
docs.text: ⚠️ Important: Unstructured date ranges are still not supported by default single-date parsing. Use multiDateExpansion for deterministic list-style multi-date strings.

docs.title: Examples of What Fails
docs.text:
Fails (without multiDateExpansion): - "May 8 - 24, 2026" ← Date range - "June 6 & 7, 2026" ← Multiple dates with ampersand - "June 27 - July 19, 2026" ← Cross-month range - "TBD" or "Call for dates" ← Unparseable text - "Ongoing" ← Non-datetime text

Succeeds (single dates parse cleanly): - "April 18, 2026" ✓ - "05/30/2026" ✓ - "2026-12-13" ✓ - "December 13, 2025" ✓

docs.title: Debug Strategy When Parse Count is Low
docs.text:
1. Run test-fetch and check validation.totalEventsParsed vs. expected count on source page
  2. If discrepancy exists, compare sampleEvents against the source
  3. Common cause: Date format uses ranges or special text that cannot parse
  4. Manual verification: Does each visible event have a single, standard date format?

docs.title: Workarounds
docs.text:
Option 1: Expand one card into multiple occurrences (recommended)

Use multiDateExpansion in HtmlLite parser config:

"multiDateExpansion": {
  "enabled": true,
  "sourceField": "startTime",
  "defaultTime": "7:30 PM",
  "defaultTimeZone": "America/Los_Angeles",
  "fallbackMode": "legacySingle",
  "limits": {
    "maxOccurrencesPerCard": 12,
    "maxExpandedEventsPerRun": 500,
    "maxParseFailuresPerCard": 3
  }
}

This enables one-card-to-many-events fan-out for supported multi-date list formats.

Option 2: Extract only the first date from a range

"fieldTransforms": {
  "startTime": [
    { "type": "ReplaceLiteral", "value": " - ", "replacement": " RANGE_SEP " },
    { "type": "ReplaceLiteral", "value": " RANGE_SEP ", "replacement": "|" }
  ]
}

Then use regex or post-processing to extract text before the pipe.

Option 3: Use detail page enrichment If list pages show date ranges but detail pages have specific start/end times: - Set list startTime to a literal: placeholder - Enable detailPage.enabled: true - Map actual dates in detailPage.detailMappings

Option 4: Create separate sources For venue+date combinations, create distinct sources: - Source 1: Events happening June 6 - Source 2: Events happening June 7

(Use filters or pagination to isolate by date)

docs.title: Normalizing a.m./p.m. Abbreviations
docs.text:
Standard date parsing does not recognize a.m. or p.m. — it requires AM/PM. If the source uses dotted abbreviations, normalize them with ReplaceLiteral transforms before any date parsing occurs.

Also strip connector words such as at that appear between the date and time string.

"fieldTransforms": {
  "startTime": [
    { "type": "ReplaceLiteral", "value": " at ", "replacement": " " },
    { "type": "ReplaceLiteral", "value": "p.m.", "replacement": "PM" },
    { "type": "ReplaceLiteral", "value": "a.m.", "replacement": "AM" },
    { "type": "CollapseWhitespace" }
  ]
}

docs.title: Multi-Date Strings — First Date vs Expansion
docs.text:
Some performing arts sites encode multiple performance dates in a single string, for example:

Saturday, April 11, 2026 at 7:00 p.m. & Sunday, April 12, 2026 at 3:00 p.m.

There are two supported patterns:

  1. Preferred: use multiDateExpansion to create one event per occurrence.
  2. Fallback: keep first-date-only transforms when you intentionally want one representative occurrence.

First-date-only transform example:

"fieldTransforms": {
  "startTime": [
    { "type": "RegexReplace", "value": " & .*$", "replacement": "" },
    { "type": "ReplaceLiteral", "value": " at ", "replacement": " " },
    { "type": "ReplaceLiteral", "value": "p.m.", "replacement": "PM" },
    { "type": "ReplaceLiteral", "value": "a.m.", "replacement": "AM" },
    { "type": "CollapseWhitespace" }
  ]
}

Note: This chain captures only the first performance date. For one-occurrence-per-performance output inside HtmlLite, prefer multiDateExpansion.

docs.title: Composition With Detail Occurrence Matching
docs.text:
When both multiDateExpansion and detailPage.occurrenceSelector are configured:

  1. multiDateExpansion determines event count
  2. detailPage.occurrenceSelector refines the matching expanded event
  3. Detail occurrence matching does not fan out additional events

This precedence keeps behavior deterministic and avoids duplicate ownership of fan-out logic.

docs.title: Default Behavior
docs.text:
• EndTime defaults to StartTime + 1 hour when no endTime mapping is provided
  • IsAllDay defaults to false

docs.title: Invalid request payload
docs.text:
Usually means schemaDefinition was sent as an object instead of a JSON string.

Fix: - serialize schemaDefinition as a compact JSON string before submission - verify request body uses schemaDefinition: "{...}" rather than nested object

docs.title: schemaDefinition must be v3 with schemaVersion=3
docs.text:
This means the payload is using legacy flat schema format.

Fix:

  • add schemaVersion: 3
  • wrap parser config under pipeline.calendar.parser
  • add pipeline.event
  • follow v3 migration guide

docs.title: phase 2 scaffolding currently supports only pipeline.event.input.field = eventUrl
docs.text:
This means event-stage input is using a field name other than eventUrl.

Fix:

  • map eventUrl in calendar mappings
  • use "field": "eventUrl" in pipeline.event.input
  • see v3 event input constraints

docs.title: pipeline.calendar.type must be "Html" for HtmlLite sources
docs.text:
A common schema validation failure occurs when contributors set pipeline.calendar.type to "HtmlLite" inside the schemaDefinition. The runtime rejects this value.

The correct distinction:

Field Correct value Top-level source type (submission envelope) "HtmlLite" pipeline.calendar.type (inside schemaDefinition) "Html"

Fix: in your schemaDefinition, set pipeline.calendar.type to "Html". The outer submission field type stays "HtmlLite".

See the v3 Pipeline Examples for a minimum-shape reference.

docs.title: JSON endpoint returns HTML string instead of event objects
docs.text:
Some endpoints return Content-Type: application/json but the payload body is an HTML string rather than structured event objects. This is common with WordPress wp-json wrappers where the body field contains raw HTML markup.

Decision rule:

  • If the JSON response contains structured event objects traversable with a path like $.events[*], use JsonApi.
  • If the JSON response contains an HTML string (event data is embedded HTML, not a JSON object array), treat the source as HtmlLite and parse the embedded HTML instead.

How to check: inspect the raw response body. If event records are HTML markup rather than JSON key/value objects, choose HtmlLite.

See Choose A Source Type for the full source type decision table.

docs.title: validation.totalEventsParsed = 0
docs.text: This is the #1 source creation issue. Events silently drop when required fields fail to parse.

docs.title: Diagnostic Checklist (in order)
docs.text:
1. Verify eventCardSelector matches DOM nodes
  2. Test in browser console: document.querySelectorAll('YOUR_SELECTOR')
  3. If zero results, selector is wrong
  4. Common error: CSS attribute selector [id^="prefix"] doesn't work in XPath

  5. Fix: Use XPath: .//*[starts-with(@id, "prefix")]

  6. Check title mapping returns values

  7. Verify mapping selector works on one card element

  8. If title is deeply nested, use // for any-depth matching instead of /

  9. Check if startTime parses

  10. Look at sampleEvents startTime values
  11. Common failure: Date ranges like "May 8 - 24, 2026" cause silent drops

  12. See time-handling.md for date range solutions

  13. Check validation.requiredFields

  14. Ensure all required fields are actually mapped in mappings
  15. Remove fields from requiredFields if source doesn't provide them

docs.title: Debug Workflow
docs.text:
1. Run test-fetch and compare sampleEvents output with visible events on page
  2. For each missing field, verify selector in browser
  3. Update selector and re-test until totalEventsParsed matches expected count
  4. Common XPath patterns:
  5. Any element with attribute starting with value: .//*[starts-with(@id, "prefix")]
  6. Element with exact attribute: .//div[@id="exact-id"]
  7. Any descendant: .//span or .//*[contains(@class, "text")]
  8. Get attribute value: Always ends with /@attributeName

docs.title: validation.isSuccess = false
docs.text:
• inspect validation.errorMessage in submit response
  • correct schemaDefinition and resubmit Draft

Common recovery loop: 1. fix one failure class at a time (selector, time parsing, pagination, detail link) 2. re-submit same Draft feedUrl 3. compare sampleEvents output to previous run 4. stop when parse count and sample quality are stable

If blocked by platform visibility limitations: - prefer generic platform improvements (for example, richer sample event output) over source-specific runtime branches

docs.title: Expression must evaluate to a node-set
docs.text:
XPath is returning a scalar where a node query is required. Move attribute access into ::attr(...) after selecting a node.

If using HtmlLite custom attribute syntax, prefer selector@attribute or selector::attr(attribute).

docs.title: Approved source cannot be edited via submit
docs.text: If submit returns a 400 indicating source is already approved: - do not continue retrying submit for that feedUrl - hand off to admins for approved-source change process

docs.title: Early Validation (Before Final Submission)
docs.text: Run these checks early to catch issues before submitting the schema. This saves iteration cycles.

docs.title: Selector Validation
docs.text:
1. Test eventCardSelector in isolation
  2. Run test-fetch with only eventCardSelector and required fields (title, startTime)
  3. Verify totalEventsParsed is non-zero and reasonable (matches count on source page)

  4. If zero, use browser console to verify selector works: document.querySelectorAll('.your-selector')

  5. Check for date format compatibility

  6. In sampleEvents, verify all startTime values parse cleanly
  7. Common failures:
    • Date ranges (e.g., "May 8 - 24, 2026") → Events silently dropped
    • Non-standard formats ("TBD", "Ongoing") → Silent drop

  8. If low parse count, check if source uses date ranges (see time-handling.md for workarounds)

  9. Validate mapping selectors

  10. Spot-check 3-5 sample events against source page
  11. Verify title, date, URL are correctly extracted
  12. If any field is null/empty in samples, fix selector before resubmitting

docs.title: Pre-Submission Quick Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Run test-fetch and check totalEventsParsed is non-zero
  • [ ] Review sampleEvents array from test-fetch (not just count)
  • [ ] Compare samples against 3+ visible events on source page
  • [ ] Verify date formats are single dates (not ranges)
  • [ ] Confirm selectors use XPath (not CSS like [id^="..."])
  • [ ] Check required fields have values in samples (title, startTime)

docs.title: Quality Gates Before Submission
docs.text:
Require all of the following: - submit response validation.isSuccess is true - submit response validation.totalEventsParsed is non-zero and reasonable - submit response validation.sampleEvents title, startTime, and url values are valid - event IDs are stable and not title-derived - time values are parseable and timezone assumptions are sane - pagination is configured when multiple pages exist - detail enrichment is enabled when list pages are incomplete

Field completeness gate: - compare parsed sample events against at least 3 known detail URLs - ensure expected detail fields are present when the source page provides them

Recommended additional checks: - sample events include expected city/region context - URLs resolve to canonical event pages (not list-only links) - detailPage.linkSelector resolves within the card scope - runtime flag WHENEBER_HTMLLITE_DETAIL_ENRICHMENT_ENABLED is enabled when detail mappings are expected to populate fields - when fieldTransforms are present, each transform is deterministic and low-risk (trim, collapseWhitespace, removePrefix, removeSuffix, replaceLiteral, stripWrappingQuotes, nullIfEqualsAny) - high-risk transform patterns are not used (regex/expression execution, multi-field semantic reconstruction)

docs.title: Geolocation Quality Gate
docs.text:
Before handoff, verify one of these is true:

  1. Source provides valid coordinates and sampled values are in valid latitude/longitude ranges.
  2. Source does not reliably provide valid coordinates, but mapped location and venueAddress values are complete enough for geocoding fallback.

Checklist:

  • no synthetic coordinates introduced by contributor or AI
  • coordinate order verified when arrays are used
  • location and venueAddress quality checked on at least 3 sample events when fallback is expected
  • geolocation behavior noted in handoff summary as source-coordinates-used or geocode-fallback-expected

docs.title: Submission Checklist
docs.text:
• compatibility check completed
  • schema submitted as Draft
  • schema ID and validation notes handed off to admins

For autonomous execution, also require: - final machine-readable report emitted - blockers and nextActions populated when status is Failed - retry attempts are bounded and documented

docs.title: Schema Quality Levels
docs.text: Level Expected Fields Basic title + startTime Standard title + startTime + url + location Rich title + startTime + endTime + url + location + description Premium Rich + imageUrl + venueName + venueAddress

docs.title: Minimum Acceptance Criteria
docs.text: Approve handoff readiness only when: 1. validation.isSuccess is true 2. validation.totalEventsParsed is greater than zero 3. sampled events look semantically correct for title/time/url 4. ID and time handling rules are stable across at least one pagination step (if paging exists)

docs.title: Field Completeness Matrix (Recommended)
docs.text:
Use this quick matrix against known detail URLs before handoff:

Field Expected On Source Present In Parsed Sample title yes/no yes/no startTime yes/no yes/no endTime yes/no yes/no description yes/no yes/no location yes/no yes/no venueName yes/no yes/no venueAddress yes/no yes/no imageUrl yes/no yes/no url yes/no yes/no

If parse count is non-zero but expected fields are still missing, treat as a quality failure and continue refinement.

docs.title: When To Use This Page
docs.text:
Use this page when the source is built on Wix and the event list is present in the initial HTML response.

This page is most useful when Wix component IDs are the only stable handles for repeated cards and child fields.

docs.title: Wix Decision Tree
docs.text:
Use this quick routing check before you write selectors:

  • Wix Events page with stable server-rendered data-hook attributes such as events-card, title, date, and location: use HtmlLite and prefer those data-hook selectors first.
  • Wix CMS repeater page where the only stable repeated handles are generated comp-* prefixes: use HtmlLite and match the repeated prefixes with XPath starts-with().
  • Wix shell page where the initial HTML does not contain repeated event cards and the real event data only appears in a JSON/bootstrap payload: keep investigating and prefer JsonApi if the JSON source is real and reusable.

docs.title: Platform Signatures
docs.text: Common Wix indicators: - repeated DOM nodes with IDs like comp-xxxxxxxx__item-... - card content identified by stable ID prefixes rather than semantic class names - event detail links under paths such as /event-details-registration/... - initial HTML may contain enough content for HtmlLite even when the page looks app-like in the browser

docs.title: Recommended Source Type By Scenario
docs.text:
• Use HtmlLite when repeated event cards are already present in the initial response.
  • Prefer JsonApi if the page shell loads event data from a real structured JSON endpoint.
  • Do not force CSS selectors when the stable structure is only expressible with XPath starts-with().

docs.title: Prefer data-hook Before comp-*
docs.text:
Many Wix Events pages expose semantic data-hook attributes in server-rendered HTML. When those hooks exist, they are usually a better first choice than generated component IDs.

Prefer this order: 1. stable data-hook selectors tied to event semantics 2. machine-readable attributes or explicit event metadata 3. comp-* prefix selectors when semantic hooks are missing

Typical Wix Events hooks: - events-card - title - date - location - event-full-date - event-full-location

Example Wix Events list-page schema:

{
  "eventCardSelector": "[data-hook='events-card']",
  "mappings": {
    "title": "a[data-hook='title']",
    "startTime": "[data-hook='date']",
    "location": "[data-hook='location']",
    "url": "a[data-hook='title']@href"
  },
  "validation": {
    "requiredFields": ["title", "startTime"]
  }
}

Use comp-* selectors as a fallback when the page behaves more like a Wix CMS repeater and does not expose stable semantic hooks.

docs.title: Event Card Selector
docs.text:
Wix uses stable ID prefixes. CSS selector [id^="prefix"] does not translate directly to the HtmlLite XPath-based parser path, so use XPath starts-with().

Correct pattern:

"eventCardSelector": ".//*[starts-with(@id, \"comp-mcsmgbbs__\")]"

docs.title: Title, Time, And URL Mappings
docs.text:
{
  "mappings": {
    "title": ".//*[starts-with(@id, \"comp-mcsn738v__\")]//span",
    "startTime": ".//*[starts-with(@id, \"comp-jfx5gg4w__\")]/text()",
    "url": ".//a[1]/@href"
  }
}

docs.title: Typical Wix Card Shape
docs.text:
<div id="comp-mcsmgbbs__item-abc123">
  <div id="comp-mcsn738v__item-abc123">
    <span>Event Title</span>
  </div>
  <div id="comp-jfx5gg4w__item-abc123">
    May 24, 2026 at 7:00pm
  </div>
  <a href="/event-detail?id=abc123">View Details</a>
</div>

docs.title: Datetime Pitfalls And Preferred Source Of Truth
docs.text:
Preferred extraction order for Wix sources: 1. structured datetime attributes or explicit event metadata 2. stable date/time text inside the repeated card 3. detail-page fields when list text is incomplete

Common pitfalls: - visible date text may include ranges or marketing copy that does not parse cleanly - .text() can produce multiple text nodes when the component has nested spans - component IDs are stable by prefix but not by full generated suffix

docs.title: Anti-Patterns To Avoid
docs.text:
• Do not use raw CSS [id^="..."] syntax when the parser expects XPath.
  • Do not lock selectors to the full generated component ID including the instance suffix.
  • Do not assume the first text node is parseable without checking whitespace and range formatting.

docs.title: Validation Checklist
docs.text:
• verify parse count is close to the visible number of cards
  • inspect sampleEvents for missing or duplicated titles caused by broad prefix matches
  • verify startTime parses consistently across multiple cards, not just the first one
  • compare parsed URLs against visible detail links

docs.title: Troubleshooting And Fallbacks
docs.text:
• If XPath matches too broadly, add child predicates or additional starts-with() constraints.
  • If text extraction returns null or multiple fragments, target the inner span or the first text node explicitly.
  • If list-page times are ranges such as May 8 - 24, 2026, use the guidance in time-handling.md.
  • If the list is teaser-only, enable detail-page enrichment instead of overfitting card selectors.
  • If a Wix Events detail page is available, prefer event-full-date and event-full-location over generic visible text blocks.

docs.title: Minimal Working Example
docs.text:
{
  "eventCardSelector": ".//*[starts-with(@id, \"comp-mcsmgbbs__\")]",
  "mappings": {
    "title": ".//*[starts-with(@id, \"comp-mcsn738v__\")]//span",
    "startTime": ".//*[starts-with(@id, \"comp-jfx5gg4w__\")]/text()",
    "url": ".//a[1]/@href"
  },
  "validation": {
    "requiredFields": ["title", "startTime"]
  }
}

docs.title: AI Runbook Notes
docs.text: When an AI agent is onboarding a Wix source: 1. Confirm the event cards exist in the first HTML response. 2. Check for stable data-hook selectors before inspecting comp-* prefixes. 3. If data-hook selectors are absent, identify stable component ID prefixes from repeated cards, not one-off wrapper IDs. 4. Build the minimal schema with title, url, and parseable startTime. 5. Validate against multiple sample cards before adding detail-page enrichment. 6. Escalate to JsonApi only if the real event data lives outside the initial HTML.

docs.title: Clark County Saffire adapter
docs.text: clark-saffire is a Clark-only, code-owned adapter, not a general Saffire integration or a workflow scripting language. The source type is HtmlLite; feedUrl must be exactly https://www.clarkcoeventcenter.com/events.

docs.title: Contract
docs.text:
{
  "schemaVersion": 3,
  "pipeline": {
    "calendar": {
      "type": "Html",
      "fetch": { "method": "GET" },
      "adapter": {
        "name": "clark-saffire",
        "options": {
          "maxDates": 200,
          "maxRequests": 100,
          "maxEvents": 100,
          "maxElapsedSeconds": 180,
          "maxTotalResponseBytes": 20000000
        }
      },
      "parser": {}
    },
    "event": { "type": "None", "input": { "mode": "none" }, "parser": {} }
  },
  "validation": { "minEventsPerFetch": 1 }
}

All five options are required. Bounds: dates 1–200, requests 3–100, event-day records 1–100, elapsed seconds 5–180, aggregate decoded response bytes 8,192–20,000,000. Each response is independently capped at 2,000,000 bytes (or a lower transport configuration limit). The effective runtime/ preview event cap can be lower; overflow fails rather than truncating.

No custom headers (even an empty header block), authentication, bodies, origins, URLs, selectors, routing, enrichment stages or extra configuration are allowed. This is the only adapter allowlisted for community test-fetch/submission; other adapters remain unavailable there. Anonymous pre-production submission/approval semantics are unchanged.

docs.title: Discovery, transport and identity
docs.text:
1. Fetch the HTML listing. Extract exactly one inline var eventDays = new Array("MM/dd/yyyy",...) bootstrap as a JSON string list, never executing JavaScript. Invalid, duplicate, unordered or excessive dates fail. Dates may span years; none are hard-coded.
  2. Preserve publisher ordering and POST batches of at most five dates to /services/eventsservice.asmx/GetEventDaysByList. Adapter code owns the exact public request shape, including string "false" filter flags and boolean searchInDescription. The existing shared method/jsonBody transport sends application/json; charset=utf-8.
  3. Require object-valued d and consume d.Days[].Times[].Items[]. Every requested date must appear exactly once with at least one item. DateString is a calendar bucket; the ASMX epoch date is not a Pacific clock.
  4. Fetch each distinct same-origin /events/{year}/{slug} detail once per execution. There is no persistent detail cache or stale-on-error reuse.
  5. Identity is clark_{EventID}_{YYYY-MM-DD}_{sorted-EventItemIDs}. Identical repeated identities deduplicate; conflicting duplicates fail. Multiple conflicting sessions without distinct publisher item identities are unsupported, not collapsed to one event.

Preview and worker always use the DNS-guarded public transport, HTTPS, fixed origin/path allowlist, no redirects, no proxy, no cookie storage and no credentials. A linked deadline bounds the entire execution, including body reads, and caller cancellation propagates.

docs.title: Authoritative schedules and completeness
docs.text:
The global ingestion schedule policy applies, not a Cinema/PDXLAN title or publisher-ID exception. The same policy runs in preview and worker execution.

The detail page must supply consistent meta[itemprop=startDate/endDate] and one itemprop=description region. Month/day prose is anchored only to these publisher years, never the current year or URL year. A date outside the metadata range fails.

  • Date-specific daily prose takes precedence over shared ASMX hours, including different closing hours on different days. Overrides are logged.
  • Explicit Hours:/Times: ranges can apply across the metadata interval. Otherwise an explicitly specified, internally consistent service range supplies the clocks.
  • Published clocks need explicit meridiem. Abbreviated 3-8pm or 4:00 - 6:00pm is accepted only when both clocks independently agree with the fully explicit public service range and its numeric start.
  • An explicit start with no end receives one elapsed hour and the shared estimated-end disclaimer once, after enrichment. Actual published ends win. Approximate durations are not treated as authoritative ends.
  • Date-labelled program titles without clocks do not override a shared showtime. Actual daily clock overrides still take precedence.
  • Explicit all-day and verified event dates without any published clocks use Pacific local midnight to next local midnight (exclusive), including 23/25-hour days. Each inventory day remains a separate occurrence; the whole multi-day metadata interval is not duplicated on every day.
  • Doors/early entry do not establish performance starts. Unsupported clock evidence, overnight ranges, DST gaps/folds, ambiguous/multiple daily schedules, unmatched daily clock labels and unknown formats still fail explicitly.

Any unresolved occurrence fails the entire source: no partial success, sample, snapshot writes or publication. Diagnostics identify occurrence and category without including response bodies, headers or session identifiers. Community preview exposes the adapter's bounded safe schedule diagnostics; other public errors retain the generic error response.

docs.title: Current source readiness
docs.text:
Anonymous live verification on 2026-10-19 with the user-approved global policy confirmed 40 dates, 64 event-day records, 27 event IDs, including 20 structured-time records. Worker and preview each validated 64/64, with zero unresolved records. Nine Cinema occurrences use the disclosed one-hour estimate; four clockless PDXLAN dates are all-day. These are observations, not policy IDs or a fixed future coverage expectation.

All 64 stable occurrence IDs were unique, all local dates matched inventory, and there were no overlapping daily duplicates. All 64 mocked worker snapshots matched mapped output; all ten preview samples matched core/detail fields. Replay added zero new snapshots and updated the same 64.

The package is locally ready for hosted validation after deployment. Hosted support has not been verified. Both API and worker require deployment of the adapter/allowlist and global policy before hosted preview; no Draft, submission, activation, deployment or backfill was performed.

docs.title: First response and reliability
docs.text:
No internal retry loop: transport failures fail immediately. A worker retry restarts discovery and all public reads. Stable publisher identities make successful replay idempotent through existing snapshot upsert behavior. Failure before adapter completion produces a failed run and no snapshots.

Use source identifier, stage, outcome, retry count, failure category and correlation identifier to isolate discovery, inventory, or daily_schedule. Suggested alert thresholds for future operation:

  • any completeness/parse failure (expected complete success rate 100%);
  • three consecutive failures or more than five retries/source/15 minutes;
  • any dead-letter growth if a dead-letter queue is introduced (this adapter has no queue or replay endpoint);
  • freshness lag greater than two configured poll intervals.

Contain repeated work by leaving the source unactivated; inspect the specific stage and safe occurrence IDs, compare current public schedules, fix fixtures/configuration if warranted, and rerun preview followed by one normal ingestion cycle. Do not omit problematic events to recover.

docs.title: v3 Event Input Constraints
docs.text:
The backend HTML/JSON detail executor supports:

  • none: no detail stage.
  • calendarFieldUrl: read the URL from the named calendar field.
  • fixedUrl: substitute calendar fields into urlTemplate.

For example, a listing link /events/123 can be made absolute without a backend URL-resolution change:

"input": {
  "mode": "fixedUrl",
  "urlTemplate": "https://example.org{{eventUrl}}"
}

calendarFieldUrl requires an already absolute HTTP(S) URL in its field:

"input": { "mode": "calendarFieldUrl", "field": "eventUrl" }

This backend executor does not resolve relative links using baseUrl or the feed URL. Do not assume older contributor test-fetch/scaffolding behavior applies to stored-schema tests and worker execution.

Both modes apply limits.sameHostOnly (default true) against the feed host before detail requests. Non-HTTP(S) URLs are rejected. maxRequestsPerRun bounds HTML fetch attempts, including failures. These checks do not implement a new redirect-host policy; redirects retain the existing HTTP client behavior.

The same effective calendar headers, restricted-header exclusions, timeout, and response-size bounds are used for listing and detail requests in stored-schema tests and runtime workers. See HTML detail extraction for occurrence scoping, transforms, fallback, identity, and minimum-count semantics.

docs.title: EventON source adapter
docs.text:
Select the compiled, allowlisted adapter with pipeline.calendar.adapter.name: "eventon" and its options. There is no assembly, class-name, script, or arbitrary plugin loading. Omitting adapter preserves the existing JSON/HTML/ICS/RSS execution paths. Unknown adapters and options fail.

Use schema version 3, calendar type Html, an empty calendar parser: {}, and event stage {"type":"None","input":{"mode":"none"},"parser":{}}. Adapter execution owns projection and monthly traversal: do not configure generic parser mappings, authentication, pagination, routing, or detail stages alongside it. fetch.method, if supplied, must be GET (bootstrap); monthly read-only POSTs are adapter-owned, not generic schema-defined write operations.

Required options:

Option Meaning futureMonths Explicit integer 1–24, including the current source-local month. No default; ask the source owner. timeZone Supported timezone, preferably IANA, for exact local month boundaries. allowedOrigins 1–10 explicit HTTPS origins; all adapter URLs must additionally equal the feed origin including port. maxRequests Integer 2–25, at least futureMonths + 1. One bootstrap GET plus one POST per month. maxEvents Whole-window unique occurrence limit 1–5000, also bounded by the server limit. Overflow fails without publishing partial data.

Optional venue: {name,address,evidenceUrl} is an explicit source-wide fact for a verified single-venue calendar. Record official provenance when authoring it. The adapter prefers event-card location, then this fact; missing both fails, never TBD. Do not use this to hide multi-venue data loss. Evidence URLs must be same-origin HTTPS; they are provenance, not automatically fetched assertions. Descriptions come only from the matching card's .eventon_desc_in, never the page sidebar, venue biography, or a fallback string.

Each invocation GETs the public calendar page and refreshes data-sc and public evo_general_params nonces in memory. The discovered evo_ajax_url template must pass origin checks. It posts URL-encoded month-specific shortcode fields to the public eventon_get_events operation. Request size is bounded by bootstrap response limits, config field limits, and request/event caps. Redirects and cookies are disabled; standard client request logging is disabled for this named transport to avoid query disclosure. Existing restricted-header policy applies identically in stored-schema tests and runtime. Authorization and stored X-WP-Nonce are not forwarded by this public adapter.

The envelope must have status: "GOOD", json occurrence inventory, and html. Every occurrence _ID must uniquely match event_ + _ID in the HTML cards; counts and identities must agree. Authoritative unix_start/unix_end override HTML dates and base-event dates, including repeats and DST. Stable IDs never depend on array ordering. Identical cross-month occurrences deduplicate; conflicts fail. Empty months do not stop traversal. validation.minEventsPerFetch applies once across the complete window before freshness filtering, not per month. For adapters, this is the only root validation option: event caps belong in adapter.options.maxEvents, and required fields are enforced by the adapter, not an ignored generic requiredFields list.

All-day Unix intervals are preserved exactly (EventON can publish inclusive 23:59:59 ends). A DST all-day interval may be 23 or 25 hours rather than 24. The date-only HTML startDate marker identifies all-day presentation only; its date/offset does not determine the authoritative instants. The internal all-day flag propagates through ingestion snapshots and the existing published event schedule flag without changing endpoint DTOs. Non-adapter paths retain their existing default behavior. Inclusive end semantics are not silently changed.

The runtime bootstrap payload-hash shortcut is disabled for adapters, because an unchanged shell says nothing about monthly responses, configuration changes, or rolling-month progression. No internal retries are added: existing worker retry policy reruns the whole read, refreshes config, and upserts stable occurrence identities. Any month failure aborts before persistence.

No endpoint DTO changes are required. The schema contract is source configuration, so validate it against source-schema-v3.schema.json before handoff. Both the stored-schema test service and ingestion service call the same executor/adapter.

docs.title: HTML Detail Extraction and Occurrences
docs.text: The backend v3 HTML executor uses pipeline.event.type = "Html" and pipeline.event.parser for detail extraction. Put mappings and transforms there, not in the obsolete pipeline.calendar.parser.detailPage block. Do not configure both paths or supply placeholder dates to make unscheduled cards look valid.

docs.title: Single-event enrichment
docs.text: Without expansion: "fanOut", mappings run against the detail document and produce one merged event per calendar seed. Non-empty detail values override calendar values; missing/empty detail values retain calendar values. A failed detail fetch may fall back to a genuinely scheduled calendar seed.

docs.title: Multiple occurrences
docs.text:
{
  "type": "Html",
  "input": {
    "mode": "fixedUrl",
    "urlTemplate": "https://example.org{{eventUrl}}"
  },
  "limits": { "sameHostOnly": true, "maxRequestsPerRun": 10 },
  "parser": {
    "expansion": "fanOut",
    "occurrenceSelector": ".schedule",
    "mappings": {
      "startDate": ".date",
      "startTime": ".time",
      "timeZone": "literal:America/Los_Angeles",
      "description": "xpath=(//div[@class='description'])[1]",
      "location": "xpath=(//div[@class='venue'])[1]"
    },
    "fieldTransforms": {
      "startDate": [{ "type": "collapseWhitespace" }],
      "startTime": [
        { "type": "replaceLiteral", "value": " until ", "replacement": "-" },
        { "type": "trim" }
      ]
    }
  }
}
  • occurrenceSelector is required for HTML fan-out and accepts CSS or node-selecting XPath (optionally prefixed with xpath=). No matching nodes means no occurrences.
  • Mappings run relative to each selected occurrence. Use . for its text, @attribute for its attribute, CSS such as a@href, or relative XPath.
  • Absolute XPath (//... or /...) reads document-level metadata even while processing an occurrence. Parenthesized XPath such as (//div[@class='venue'])[1] selects the first document-level match. XPath must select nodes, not scalar string(...) / normalize-space(...) results.
  • fieldTransforms has the same ordered operations as HTML calendar mappings: trim, collapseWhitespace, replaceLiteral, and regexReplace. Replacement operations use value, replacement, and optional ignoreCase. Regex uses .NET syntax ($1 for capture replacements) and a bounded timeout. Unknown transforms fail extraction rather than silently falling back.
  • HTML entities are decoded before transforms.
  • Map startDate, startTime, and timeZone for local times. Time ranges can share a trailing meridiem (3:00-6:00 PM) or specify both (9:00am to 4:00pm). A missing/unparseable schedule is skipped; dates are never synthesized. A local date must include a year; bare clock values cannot become "today" via date parsing.
  • Fan-out IDs use the merged id (falling back to detail URL) plus :: and the UTC start timestamp in round-trip format. Reordering nodes does not change IDs. Identical identities at the same start within a seed are deduplicated. A changed start creates a new identity; distinct simultaneous events need distinct mapped IDs.
  • A failed/blocked detail fetch in fan-out produces no seed fallback occurrence. Request limits count attempted requests, including failures. There is no immediate detail retry; later source runs can fetch again.
  • maxEventsPerFetch limits returned occurrences, not just calendar cards.

Existing JSON eventArrayPath fan-out and index-based JSON identities are unchanged.

docs.title: Source coverage and location quality
docs.text:
Validate every listing card against its current detail page, not a fixed expected event count from an older snapshot. One annual event can have multiple simultaneous sessions at different venues. Map a distinct id for each such session (for example, its explicit park name) so the shared start timestamp does not collapse them. Map a shared page date with absolute XPath and per-session time/location with relative XPath when that matches the source structure.

Do not use a navigation/sidebar contact address as proof of an event's venue. Prefer the venue stated in the event body. If a specific venue is not published, a publisher-supported city-level calendar location default may be retained by the normal non-empty merge policy. Document that this is city-only and do not populate a fabricated specific venue/address. Retrospective results without a next date/time schedule must not create new occurrences.

docs.title: Yearless HTML calendar dates
docs.text:
Prefer an authoritative year from the publisher when available. For a recognizable month/day with no year (for example Oct 15, Thu, Oct 15, 15 Oct, or 10/15), the HTML parser compares that month/day with today's calendar date in the mapped timeZone (America/Los_Angeles for Pacific sources; an omitted timezone defaults to UTC). Today or a later month/day uses the current local year; an earlier month/day uses the next local year. The event's clock time does not affect this choice, so a show earlier today remains in this year. Optional weekday text does not establish a year.

Explicit-year dates, including past dates, and full absolute timestamps retain their supplied year. Missing dates and time-only date fields cannot borrow today's date. A selected year in which the date is invalid (such as yearless Feb 29 in a non-leap year) produces a parse failure and skips that occurrence, following the existing invalid-date policy. No date is clamped or moved to a later leap year. An explicitly mapped yearless end that cannot be parsed also skips the occurrence rather than silently substituting a default end.

This is a simple fallback, not sequence inference: a genuinely past yearless event can be promoted into next year. It applies independently to split HTML start/end calendar dates, not JSON or ICS parsing. The normal 24-hour freshness filter below is unchanged.

Root validation.minEventsPerFetch is enforced by stored-schema tests and runtime ingestion. It counts successfully parsed occurrences with non-empty title and location before the freshness filter, within configured request/event limits. It does not count listing cards or require a minimum number of future events. Past-only calendars can therefore pass and return zero upcoming events.

Failure diagnostics include required, parsed, validBeforeFreshnessFilter, and upcomingAfterFilter. Runtime fails before snapshot writes or publication. An omitted minimum preserves empty-result success; 0 explicitly permits it. The compact test response count/sample remains freshness-filtered (end time within the past 24 hours or later). Root requiredFields is not an arbitrary field-rule engine in this executor; the core title/location policy is fixed.

HTML detail sources are re-extracted even when the listing payload hash is unchanged, since detail schedules can change independently. Configured minimums are also rechecked on unchanged payloads. Inspect representative descriptions, locations, source URLs, and both ends of each schedule, not just card counts.

docs.title: Journey Theater adapter
docs.text:
Requires the Journey adapter backend deployment before storing this schema. Select code-owned pipeline.calendar.adapter.name: "journey". Feed URL must be https://journeytheater.org/. This is one logical source discovering publisher-linked child calendars, not source-record creation or a general-purpose crawler.

{
  "schemaVersion": 3,
  "pipeline": {
    "calendar": {
      "type": "Html",
      "fetch": { "method": "GET" },
      "adapter": {
        "name": "journey",
        "options": {
          "futureMonths": 12,
          "maxRequests": 30,
          "maxFeeds": 10,
          "maxEvents": 1000
        }
      },
      "parser": {}
    },
    "event": { "type": "None", "input": { "mode": "none" }, "parser": {} }
  },
  "validation": { "minEventsPerFetch": 1 }
}

Options are required integers: futureMonths 1–24 (rolling months ahead), maxRequests 4–50, maxFeeds 1–20, maxEvents 1–5000. Event count is additionally server-capped. Optional root validation accepts only minEventsPerFetch. No generic mappings, routing, auth, plugin names, arbitrary origins or ticket API. Unrecognized options fail.

docs.title: Dynamic discovery and classification
docs.text:
Each execution rediscovers the official event-calendar iframe's Google calendar src IDs, including base64 IDs. New embedded IDs need no schema change. The page's public WordPress representation is used if its rendered path returns 403/404/503. Do not infer one calendar per production: the publisher currently uses program/area calendars.

Current homepage .showcard-dates cards provide the public production catalogue. When root returns 403, the Journey adapter requests the public WordPress pages?slug=shows representation through the shared bounded transport; the adapter discovers its ID, follows all published child-page collection pages and selects production templates. There are no fixed show IDs/titles/calendar IDs in configuration or code. This fallback may lack a homepage-only advertised production that has no published child page. The public-page catalogue is best effort, not a guarantee of complete coverage.

Event summary must match one catalogue title (including an explicitly bounded performance prefix/suffix or a longer name starting with a meaningful published short title), and explicit season years constrain fallback matches. Rehearsals, auditions, callbacks, classes/camps, training/tech, parties, office, school-day and cue-to-cue entries are excluded. Unknown/ambiguous entries are omitted with warning counts; a failed/empty discovery is an error, not success. Unlinked calendars, arbitrary new layouts, unusual show names containing excluded activity words, and publicly eligible showcases without clear catalogue matches may require maintenance. Title matching is intentionally pragmatic, not AI-based.

docs.title: Schedules, details and missing venues
docs.text:
Ical.Net expands official calendar dates in a bounded window, preserving RRULE/RDATE/EXDATE, recurrence overrides, cancellation and DST. The result is independent occurrences, with no residual RRULE sent to the domain. IDs namespace calendar identity + UID + original recurrence slot (RECURRENCE-ID for moved instances), never array position. Independent calendars are not fuzzy-deduplicated.

Official calendar timestamps win. Ticket schedules are not fetched or merged. Previously observed ticket/calendar conflicts therefore do not alter these events; the adapter cannot detect future ticket changes it never fetches. Publisher timezone for floating/date-only values is America/Los_Angeles.

Description and public URL come from the matching public show page/card, with ICS description preferred. HTML is flattened to text and scripts/styles removed. Optional description fetch failure does not discard an otherwise usable event. Venue comes only from ICS LOCATION: no office address, ticket draft or guessed shared venue. An absent venue uses the existing nonblank domain sentinel TBD, with no fabricated venue/address/coordinates and an explicit missing-venue warning count. The publisher skips geocoding that sentinel. It is not a verified venue; events without coordinates may not appear in map/distance-based discovery.

docs.title: Reliability and security
docs.text:
