All requests use the same bounded shared transport as test-fetch/runtime. Only fixed HTTPS publisher page paths and validated Google public group-calendar paths are fetchable; arbitrary iframe origins, ports, userinfo, redirects and cookies are rejected/disabled. Authorization/Cookie/nonce headers are not forwarded. Named transport decompresses bounded response streams; there is no browser, external process, private-address URL input or arbitrary script execution.

Bootstrap hash-skip is disabled: unchanged page text does not imply unchanged child feeds. A required calendar fetch/parse failure aborts before snapshots, avoiding a smaller successful replacement inventory. Request/feed/event caps fail explicitly. No internal retry loop: an authorized later retry repeats discovery and upserts stable identities. Optional enrichment and classification omissions are warning-counted and intentionally best effort.

Logs carry the existing SourceId/CorrelationId scopes and stage/outcome/retry count/failure category plus discovered feeds, productions, emitted/excluded, unmatched, missing venue and missing-description counts. Review warnings before authorizing ingestion; schema-test success alone does not certify full coverage.

docs.title: Source Schema v3 Migration Guide
docs.text: Use this guide when converting legacy flat schemaDefinition payloads to v3.

docs.title: Current requirement
docs.text:
New contributor submissions must use:

  • schemaVersion: 3
  • pipeline.calendar
  • pipeline.event

If missing, requests fail with: schemaDefinition must be v3 with schemaVersion=3.

docs.title: Flat -> v3 mapping
docs.text:
Legacy shape (flat HtmlLite example):

{
  "eventCardSelector": "...",
  "mappings": {
    "title": "...",
    "startTime": "..."
  },
  "validation": {
    "requiredFields": ["title", "startTime"]
  }
}

v3 shape:

{
  "schemaVersion": 3,
  "pipeline": {
    "calendar": {
      "type": "Html",
      "parser": {
        "eventCardSelector": "...",
        "mappings": {
          "title": "...",
          "startTime": "..."
        }
      }
    },
    "event": {
      "type": "Html",
      "input": {
        "mode": "calendarFieldUrl",
        "field": "eventUrl"
      },
      "parser": {
        "mappings": {}
      },
      "limits": {
        "sameHostOnly": true,
        "maxRequestsPerRun": 5
      }
    }
  },
  "validation": {
    "requiredFields": ["title", "startTime"]
  }
}

docs.title: Migration checklist
docs.text:
1. Add schemaVersion: 3.
  2. Move parser config under pipeline.calendar.parser.
  3. Set pipeline.calendar.type to one of: Ics, Rss, Json, Html.
  4. Add pipeline.event using an allowed pair from Type Pair Reference.
  5. If using calendarFieldUrl, map eventUrl in calendar mappings and set event input field to eventUrl.
  6. Run POST /api/source-schemas/test-fetch before submission.

docs.title: Common migration mistakes
docs.text:
• Keeping flat fields at root (eventCardSelector, mappings) instead of inside pipeline.calendar.parser
  • Using disallowed pair Html -> None
  • Using pipeline.event.input.field: "url" instead of "eventUrl" in current phase-2 scaffolding
  • Sending schemaDefinition as object instead of JSON string in request envelope

docs.title: Minimal Valid Schemas by Type
docs.text: Use these templates as a starting point. Add fields incrementally and validate after each change.

docs.title: Html -> Html (HtmlLite Sources — Minimum Valid v3 Pipeline)
docs.text:
Use this pipeline pair for HtmlLite sources. For v3, Html -> None is not allowed by the current security allowlist.

pipeline.calendar.type for HtmlLite sources

The top-level source type field in the submission envelope is "HtmlLite".

The inner pipeline.calendar.type inside schemaDefinition must be "Html" — not "HtmlLite". Using "HtmlLite" as the inner calendar type fails v3 runtime validation.

Note: During current phase-2 scaffolding, pipeline.event.input.field must be eventUrl.

{
  "schemaVersion": 3,
  "pipeline": {
    "calendar": {
      "type": "Html",
      "fetch": {
        "requestHeaders": {
          "User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64)"
        }
      },
      "parser": {
        "eventCardSelector": ".event-item",
        "mappings": {
          "title": "h2",
          "startTime": ".date",
          "eventUrl": "a@href"
        }
      }
    },
    "event": {
      "type": "Html",
      "input": { "mode": "calendarFieldUrl", "field": "eventUrl" },
      "parser": { "mappings": {} },
      "limits": {
        "sameHostOnly": true,
        "maxRequestsPerRun": 5
      }
    }
  },
  "validation": {
    "requiredFields": ["title", "startTime"]
  }
}

docs.title: Ics -> None
docs.text:
Use Ics -> None when the ICS feed provides complete event data and no HTML detail-page enrichment is needed. This is the correct combination for most ICS sources.

Common mistake: Setting event.type to "Html" for a plain ICS feed that requires no detail-page fetch will fail validation. Use "None" unless you need to follow eventUrl to fetch per-event HTML pages.

{
  "schemaVersion": 3,
  "pipeline": {
    "calendar": {
      "type": "Ics",
      "parser": {}
    },
    "event": {
      "type": "None",
      "input": {
        "mode": "none"
      },
      "parser": {}
    }
  },
  "validation": {
    "requiredFields": ["title", "startTime"]
  }
}

docs.title: Ics -> None (with fieldTransforms)
docs.text:
Use this variant when ICS fields are mostly correct but require deterministic cleanup (for example, Teams links prefixed in LOCATION).

{
  "schemaVersion": 3,
  "pipeline": {
    "calendar": {
      "type": "Ics",
      "parser": {
        "fieldTransforms": {
          "location": [
            {
              "type": "regexReplace",
              "value": "^\\s*https://teams\\.microsoft\\.com[^,]*(?:,\\s*)?(.*)$",
              "replacement": "$1"
            },
            { "type": "trim" },
            { "type": "collapseWhitespace" }
          ]
        }
      }
    },
    "event": {
      "type": "None",
      "input": {
        "mode": "none"
      },
      "parser": {}
    }
  },
  "validation": {
    "requiredFields": ["title", "startTime"]
  }
}

fieldTransforms is optional and should be used for cleanup only, not for reconstructing missing required fields.

docs.title: Ics -> Html
docs.text:
{
  "schemaVersion": 3,
  "pipeline": {
    "calendar": {
      "type": "Ics",
      "parser": {}
    },
    "event": {
      "type": "Html",
      "input": {
        "mode": "calendarFieldUrl",
        "field": "eventUrl"
      },
      "parser": {
        "mappings": {
          "description": ".event-details",
          "venueAddress": ".venue-address",
          "imageUrl": ".hero img@src"
        }
      },
      "limits": {
        "sameHostOnly": true,
        "maxRequestsPerRun": 5
      }
    }
  },
  "validation": {
    "requiredFields": ["title", "startTime"]
  }
}

docs.title: Json -> Json
docs.text:
{
  "schemaVersion": 3,
  "pipeline": {
    "calendar": {
      "type": "Json",
      "parser": {
        "eventArrayPath": "$.events[*]",
        "mappings": {
          "title": "$.name",
          "startTime": "$.start",
          "eventUrl": "$.detailUrl"
        }
      }
    },
    "event": {
      "type": "Json",
      "input": {
        "mode": "calendarFieldUrl",
        "field": "eventUrl"
      },
      "parser": {
        "eventArrayPath": "$.items[*]",
        "mappings": {
          "description": "$.description",
          "venueName": "$.venue.name",
          "venueAddress": "$.venue.address"
        }
      },
      "limits": {
        "sameHostOnly": true,
        "maxRequestsPerRun": 10
      }
    }
  },
  "validation": {
    "requiredFields": ["title", "startTime"]
  }
}

docs.title: Json -> Html (Cross-Host Detail Description)
docs.text:
Use this pattern when:

  • list API host differs from public detail-page host
  • list payload has sparse or empty description
  • detail HTML contains full event body
{
  "schemaVersion": 3,
  "pipeline": {
    "calendar": {
      "type": "Json",
      "fetch": {
        "method": "Post"
      },
      "parser": {
        "eventArrayPath": "$.hits[*]",
        "mappings": {
          "id": "$.objectID",
          "title": "$.title",
          "startTime": "$.dates[*]",
          "eventUrl": "$.url",
          "venueName": "literal:The Museum",
          "venueAddress": "literal:1945 SE Water Ave, Portland, OR 97214",
          "location": "literal:1945 SE Water Ave, Portland, OR 97214"
        }
      }
    },
    "event": {
      "type": "Html",
      "input": {
        "mode": "calendarFieldUrl",
        "field": "eventUrl",
        "baseUrl": "https://omsi.edu"
      },
      "parser": {
        "mappings": {
          "description": ".container-content"
        }
      },
      "limits": {
        "sameHostOnly": false,
        "maxRequestsPerRun": 25
      }
    }
  },
  "validation": {
    "requiredFields": ["title", "startTime"]
  }
}

Notes:

  • sameHostOnly: false is required when list and detail hosts differ.
  • input.baseUrl ensures detail links resolve to the public content host.
  • detail values override defaults only when detail values are non-empty.

docs.title: Html -> Html with Multi-Date Expansion
docs.text:
Use this when one HTML event card contains multiple occurrence dates in one text field.

{
  "schemaVersion": 3,
  "pipeline": {
    "calendar": {
      "type": "Html",
      "parser": {
        "eventCardSelector": ".event-card",
        "mappings": {
          "id": "a@href",
          "title": "h3",
          "startTime": ".showings",
          "url": "a@href",
          "timeZone": "literal:America/Los_Angeles"
        },
        "multiDateExpansion": {
          "enabled": true,
          "sourceField": "startTime",
          "defaultTime": "7:30 PM",
          "defaultTimeZone": "America/Los_Angeles",
          "fallbackMode": "legacySingle",
          "limits": {
            "maxOccurrencesPerCard": 12,
            "maxExpandedEventsPerRun": 500,
            "maxParseFailuresPerCard": 3
          }
        },
        "detailPage": {
          "enabled": true,
          "linkSelector": "a@href",
          "occurrenceSelector": ".occurrence",
          "occurrenceMappings": {
            "startTime": ".occ-start::attr(datetime)",
            "endTime": ".occ-end::attr(datetime)"
          }
        }
      }
    },
    "event": {
      "type": "Html",
      "input": { "mode": "calendarFieldUrl", "field": "eventUrl" },
      "parser": { "mappings": {} },
      "limits": {
        "sameHostOnly": true,
        "maxRequestsPerRun": 10
      }
    }
  },
  "validation": {
    "requiredFields": ["title", "startTime", "url"]
  }
}

Composition rule:

  1. multiDateExpansion determines how many events are emitted from each card.
  2. detailPage.occurrenceSelector refines each emitted event.
  3. Detail occurrence matching does not change event count.

docs.title: Generic JSON POST calendar
docs.text:
Anonymous read-only JSON queries can use a typed body. This complete example uses query pagination; the literal body remains identical on every page. See JSON API request policy for limits and contributor restrictions. This does not discover or batch dates.

{
  "schemaVersion": 3,
  "pipeline": {
    "calendar": {
      "type": "Json",
      "fetch": {
        "method": "POST",
        "jsonBody": { "categoryID": 0, "includePast": false, "filters": [] },
        "pagination": {
          "strategy": "Page",
          "pageParamName": "page",
          "totalPagesPath": "$.pages"
        }
      },
      "parser": {
        "eventArrayPath": "$.events[*]",
        "mappings": {
          "id": "$.id",
          "title": "$.title",
          "startTime": "$.start",
          "location": "$.venue",
          "description": "$.description",
          "imageUrl": "$.image",
          "eventUrl": "$.url"
        }
      }
    },
    "event": { "type": "None", "input": { "mode": "none" }, "parser": {} }
  }
}

docs.title: Source Schema v3 Pipeline Overview
docs.text:
Source Schema v3 introduces a clean two-stage schemaDefinition contract:

  • calendar: fetch and parse the source calendar/list payload
  • event: enrich or transform each calendar item into final event fields

This model replaces implicit parser branching with explicit stage contracts.

All parsers and adapters follow the shared schedule policy: verified start without end is one hour with a disclosed estimate; a verified date without clocks is all-day in the source timezone. Publisher ends win.

For the audited Clark County publisher, the Clark Saffire adapter owns HTML date discovery, five-date service POST batches and authoritative daily schedules. These operations are not generic pipeline DSL features. It is the only adapter currently allowlisted for community submissions; incomplete schedules fail without partial results.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• Support flexible combinations for unexpected sources.
  • Keep one canonical execution path for test-fetch and ingestion.
  • Make parser composition explicit and statically validated.

docs.title: v3 shape
docs.text:
{
  "schemaVersion": 3,
  "pipeline": {
    "calendar": {
      "type": "Ics",
      "parser": {}
    },
    "event": {
      "type": "Html",
      "input": {
        "mode": "calendarFieldUrl",
        "field": "eventUrl"
      },
      "parser": {
        "mappings": {
          "description": ".event-description",
          "imageUrl": ".hero img@src"
        }
      },
      "limits": {
        "sameHostOnly": true,
        "maxRequestsPerRun": 5
      }
    }
  },
  "validation": {
    "requiredFields": ["title", "startTime"]
  }
}

  • Rss -> None
  • Rss -> Html
  • Rss -> Json

Combinations outside this matrix are rejected by schema validation.

docs.title: Stage contract summary
docs.text:
Calendar stage output must include enough fields for event stage input when event stage is not None.

Calendar stage fetch options may include: - fetch.authentication for bearer, API key, or basic auth - fetch.requestHeaders for non-restricted custom headers - fetch.pagination for page, offset, or cursor traversal

For the backend v3 Html executor, detail occurrence expansion belongs in pipeline.event.parser: set expansion: "fanOut", occurrenceSelector, mappings, and optional fieldTransforms. Relative mappings read the selected occurrence; absolute XPath reads document-level metadata. The obsolete calendar detailPage block is not the execution path. See HTML detail extraction for identity, missing-schedule, minimum-count, and freshness semantics.

For Ics calendar parsers, calendar parser options can include fieldTransforms for deterministic per-field cleanup after RFC 5545 parsing and before event-stage processing. This does not enable mappings for Ics.

Example Ics parser cleanup:

{
  "pipeline": {
    "calendar": {
      "type": "Ics",
      "parser": {
        "fieldTransforms": {
          "location": [
            {
              "type": "regexReplace",
              "value": "^\\s*https://teams\\.microsoft\\.com[^,]*(?:,\\s*)?(.*)$",
              "replacement": "$1"
            },
            { "type": "trim" },
            { "type": "collapseWhitespace" }
          ]
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

If no cleanup is needed, keep parser as {}.

Event stage input modes: - none - calendarFieldUrl - fixedUrl

Current implementation note: - In current phase-2 scaffolding, pipeline.event.input.field is restricted to eventUrl when event.type is Html or Json. - For calendarFieldUrl, you can optionally set pipeline.event.input.baseUrl to resolve/rebase detail links to the public content host.

docs.title: Event Input Modes Reference
docs.text:
The pipeline.event.input.mode determines how per-event details are obtained. Choose based on your source structure:

Mode Use Case Example Input Config none Events are already complete from calendar stage; no detail page needed ICS feed with full event data { "mode": "none" } calendarFieldUrl Calendar stage outputs a URL field (e.g., eventUrl); fetch detail page per event Calendar list has link to detail page in each item { "mode": "calendarFieldUrl", "field": "eventUrl" } fixedUrl All events use the same detail page URL pattern; substitute event ID into template Detail URL is predictable: https://example.com/events/{eventId} { "mode": "fixedUrl", "url": "https://example.com/events/{id}" }

docs.title: Decision Tree
docs.text:
For exact calendarFieldUrl constraints and baseUrl behavior, see Event Input Constraints.

  1. Does your calendar stage output complete event data?
  2. Yes → Keep event lightweight, but still choose an allowed pair for your calendar type
  3. For Ics and Rss, event.type: "None" is valid
  4. For Html, choose event.type: "Html" or "Json" per the allowlist

  5. No → Continue to step 2

  6. Does each calendar item have a link to its detail page?

  7. Yes → Use mode: "calendarFieldUrl"; in current phase-2 scaffolding map and use eventUrl

  8. No → Continue to step 3

  9. Can you construct detail URLs from event IDs?

  10. Yes → Use mode: "fixedUrl"; provide URL template with {id} placeholder and validate behavior in your target environment
  11. No → Check if detail page enrichment is needed; if not, use mode: "none"

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Ics -> None (Complete calendar feed)

{
  "pipeline": {
    "calendar": { "type": "Ics" },
    "event": { "type": "None", "input": { "mode": "none" } }
  }
}

Html -> Html with detail enrichment (Calendar has detail links)

{
  "pipeline": {
    "calendar": { "type": "Html", "parser": { "mappings": { "eventUrl": "a.event-link@href" } } },
    "event": { "type": "Html", "input": { "mode": "calendarFieldUrl", "field": "eventUrl" } }
  }
}

Json -> Json with fixed template (Predictable detail URLs)

{
  "pipeline": {
    "calendar": { "type": "Json" },
    "event": { "type": "Json", "input": { "mode": "fixedUrl", "url": "https://api.example.com/events/{id}" } }
  }
}

docs.title: Security defaults
docs.text:
• event.limits.sameHostOnly defaults to true.
  • event.limits.maxRequestsPerRun is required when event type is Html or Json.
  • Event URL modes must use http or https only.

docs.title: Optional source adapter
docs.text:
Tockify public calendars can select the closed tockify adapter for complete offset inventory and required rich public-detail joins. See Tockify adapter for rolling horizon/caps, epoch and recurrence identity semantics, canonical URLs, images, evidence-backed venue facts and publisher-access boundaries.

TicketWeb Event Discovery WordPress calendars can select the closed ticketweb adapter for public bootstrap/config discovery, monthly form POSTs, and JSON/popup joins. See TicketWeb adapter for the default 12-calendar-month window, required timezone/allowed origins, evidence-backed venue configuration, show-versus-doors semantics and inferred ends.

EventON public calendars can select the closed eventon adapter in pipeline.calendar.adapter. See EventON source adapter for required explicit month windows, origin restrictions, authoritative occurrence schedules, and whole-window completeness validation.

Journey Theater can select the closed journey adapter for dynamic publisher-linked Google calendar discovery. See Journey adapter for best-effort public-show classification, official ICS recurrence semantics, and the existing TBD missing-venue convention. This requires the corresponding backend deployment; it is not supported by older schema executors.

docs.title: Adapter execution boundary
docs.text:
The backend resolves adapter names through an explicit dependency-injected registry. The currently registered names are eventon, journey, ticketweb and tockify; unknown names and duplicate registrations fail closed. Each adapter validates its own typed options and owns its complete bootstrap, discovery, fallback, and parsing lifecycle. Generic HTML, JSON, RSS, and ICS schemas continue through the normal executor and do not receive adapter-specific behavior.

Both runtime ingestion and schema test-fetch use the same prepared adapter and bounded fetch service. The service applies restricted-header filtering, response size and timeout limits, safe host/path-only diagnostics, adapter-supplied URL constraints, and the named adapter HTTP client with redirects and cookies disabled. TicketWeb, EventON and Journey retain distinct URL scopes; only the EventON public nonce is forwarded as the explicit nonce header. Test-fetch success does not certify full source coverage; review adapter warnings and the source-specific validation guidance before authorizing ingestion.

docs.title: Ticketmaster public venue adapter
docs.text:
The ticketmaster code-owned adapter reads Ticketmaster's currently public, undocumented website venue-search endpoint and classifies inventory using the event page's embedded #__NEXT_DATA__ JSON. It is not the official Ticketmaster Discovery API, does not use an API key, and is not a general HTTP or pagination facility. Website behavior can change; unrecognized responses fail instead of yielding a partial calendar.

{
  "schemaVersion": 3,
  "pipeline": {
    "calendar": {
      "type": "Html",
      "fetch": { "method": "GET" },
      "adapter": {
        "name": "ticketmaster",
        "options": {
          "venueIds": ["123078", "123041"],
          "pageSize": 20,
          "maxRequests": 200,
          "maxEvents": 500
        }
      },
      "parser": {}
    },
    "event": { "type": "None", "input": { "mode": "none" }, "parser": {} }
  },
  "validation": { "minEventsPerFetch": 1 }
}

The feed URL remains the source's official https://www.ticketmaster.com/ venue or event page URL; no request is made to the feed itself. Supply the publisher's numeric venue ID(s) in venueIds. Options are closed and bounded: 1–10 distinct decimal venue IDs, the currently fixed 20-record pageSize, a whole-run maxRequests from 2–1000, and a combined inventory/output maxEvents from 1–5000. Select request/event limits using the actual source inventory, including detail-page classifications. The adapter does not contain venue IDs for any particular source.

docs.title: Fetch, pagination, and joins
docs.text:
1. For each venue, request only GET https://www.ticketmaster.com/api/search/events/venue?venueId={id}&page={zeroBasedPage}. The host, route, query key order, decimal IDs, HTTPS/default port, and zero- based page number are constrained in code. The first page's total governs exact page count and expected page cardinality (20 except for the last page).
  2. Fail the entire execution on changing/invalid totals, malformed records, duplicate identities within a venue, missing/extra page records, request or event-cap overflow, or non-progress. Identical listings repeated across configured venues deduplicate by Ticketmaster's stable 16-hex ID; conflicting versions fail.
  3. Events with publisher dates.dateDisplay of showDateTime or showDate and no cancelled, postponed, or tba flag are candidates for output. No dates are synthesized. Date-only records require publisher timezone evidence and are all-day, never midnight performances. Unscheduled records remain excluded.
  4. Fetch the canonical event page for every scheduled candidate, then parse only its single embedded <script id="__NEXT_DATA__"> JSON object. Both recognized Ticketmaster page layouts are supported: old edpData.context event objects and pageProps.eventInfo. Detail identity must match the inventory ID and a recognized classification array must be present. classifications[].type.name == "Upsell" excludes an item independent of its title. Missing, ambiguous, or malformed layouts/classification fail closed; title/prose heuristics are not used.
  5. Return nothing until all required detail requests and classification checks succeed. Stable IDs are ticketmaster_{lowercasePublisherId}. Retry/replay re-reads the venue inventory and all required details; no adapter-level retries or partial writes are introduced.

All requests are default-port HTTPS to www.ticketmaster.com and are limited to the exact inventory endpoint/query or canonical /.../event/{16-hex-id} paths. The existing adapter transport disables redirects and cookies, filters unsafe schema-supplied headers, and bounds response bytes/time. Do not add credentials, API keys, cookies, or private headers to the schema.

docs.title: Normalized fields and time semantics
docs.text:
• Title, event URL, date/time, venue, image, and inventory identity come from the public venue record. Start and explicit end timestamps must contain an offset or Z, and are normalized to UTC without reinterpreting publisher wall time. Missing end times use the shared one-hour estimate with a bottom-of-description disclaimer after enrichment. Real ends win. showDate date-only records are all-day when a publisher timezone is supplied in dates.timeZone, dates.timezone, or venue.timeZone; absent timezone evidence fails rather than inferring from geography. Unscheduled records remain excluded.
  • Venue name, address line, city, and state are projected only from that inventory record. No source-wide fallback location is invented.
  • Description is plain text from the recognized detail JSON's generalInfo.text, webInfoNoHtml, or webInfo, where present. Missing publisher descriptions remain null unless the shared estimated-end disclosure is required. No marketing prose is synthesized.
  • Classification checks use metadata, never event title, text, product labels, URL path words, or parent-event add-on references.

This website API is undocumented and may drift. Revalidate representative payloads after publisher changes. A detail or inventory parse failure is observable at the adapter stage and fails the whole run before persistence. For first response, contain repeated work for the affected source, isolate inventory/pagination/detail-classification/persistence using source and correlation scopes, repair the contract or adapter against fresh public data, and replay through the normal worker after validation. Suggested initial alert baselines are parse success below 90% over 15 minutes/20 fetches, more than five retries per source in ten minutes, sustained dead-letter growth, or freshness lag beyond twice the source cadence.

docs.title: TicketWeb WordPress calendar adapter
docs.text:
ticketweb supports the public TicketWeb Event Discovery WordPress plugin, calendar2 protocol. It is not a general TicketWeb API client, JavaScript interpreter, or arbitrary request workflow. No hostname, show title or event ID is built into the adapter.

{
  "schemaVersion": 3,
  "pipeline": {
    "calendar": {
      "type": "Html",
      "fetch": {
        "method": "GET",
        "requestHeaders": {
          "User-Agent": "Wheneber/1.0 (+https://dev.app.wheneber.com)"
        }
      },
      "adapter": {
        "name": "ticketweb",
        "options": {
          "timeZone": "America/Los_Angeles",
          "allowedOrigins": ["https://calendar.example"],
          "futureMonths": 12,
          "maxRequests": 13,
          "maxEvents": 1000,
          "venue": {
            "name": "Example Venue",
            "address": "123 Example St",
            "evidenceUrl": "https://calendar.example/"
          }
        }
      },
      "parser": {}
    },
    "event": { "type": "None", "input": { "mode": "none" }, "parser": {} }
  },
  "validation": { "minEventsPerFetch": 1 }
}

Use the publisher's calendar page as the source feed URL. The optional venue above is illustrative, not a fact suitable for a real source. Verify a single-venue calendar before supplying it. A missing published venue without this evidence-backed fact fails extraction. Do not infer event location from unrelated sidebar/contact text.

docs.title: Execution and bounds
docs.text:
1. GET the configured page with the normal shared header filter. Identify exactly one inline public get_events_for_calendar configuration. Extract bounded JS string literals for endpoint, fresh public nonce, JSON params, and standard month view; never execute JavaScript. Multiple calendars or unsupported literal/config shapes fail explicitly.
  2. Preserve the publisher's calendar/filter/presentation params. Replace stale month/year/current_datetime values using the current source-local time. Reject authentication-like params and inventory-suppressing limit/pagination, first-only, one-per-date or max-per-venue settings rather than silently discarding rows. Only page zero/no pagination is supported.
  3. POST the public action and fresh nonce as form fields to the advertised, same-origin .../wp-admin/admin-ajax.php, one local calendar month per request using [month start, next-month start). The publisher compares dates with an exclusive end, ignoring the supplied end time: using last-day 23:59:59 would silently lose that day's shows. Include the advertised standard-view/calcount/filter/mobile-list fields. FormUrlEncodedContent encodes the preserved params exactly once.
  4. Join events rows to popupdata by the tw-event-dialog-{publisherId} fragment target. The row is the schedule inventory; mobile_events and mobile list markup are alternate presentations, not additional occurrences. Missing/extra/duplicate popups, conflicting duplicate occurrences, or invalid required details fail the whole run before persistence. Equal duplicate rows deduplicate.
  5. Return normalized occurrences through the existing adapter registry. Runtime and schema test-fetch use the same prepared adapter, transport, header policy and field projection. An unchanged bootstrap does not skip AJAX extraction.

futureMonths defaults to 12 including the current month (range 1–24). For example, a run in October requests October through September of next year; it does not start today or include the following October. Empty months do not stop discovery. maxRequests defaults to months + 1 (range 2–25) and must cover the entire window. maxEvents defaults to 1000 (range 1–5000). Schema/server event caps, response byte limits, timeout and cancellation fail rather than truncate. The shared freshness filter runs after extraction and minimum-event validation.

Every requested URL must be HTTPS, without credentials or fragments, on both the exact feed origin and allowedOrigins. Bootstrap and AJAX endpoint queries are forbidden. Cookies, redirects and schema-supplied Authorization/X-WP-Nonce are disabled by the existing adapter transport. The fresh public nonce goes only in the publisher-advertised form, not an auth header. Do not save a live nonce, request body or response bootstrap in diagnostics.

docs.title: Field semantics and evidence
docs.text:
• start date + displayTime are show start, not doors. Cross-check sortkey when present, and require matching popup date/time. Dates include an explicit year. Publisher-local wall times are converted using configured timeZone; DST ambiguity/nonexistent times fail instead of guessing.
  • The observed plugin does not publish end times. The shared policy supplies start + one elapsed hour, including midnight/DST crossings, and appends a disclosure once after enrichment. Explicit local end in yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss or yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss is preserved and validated.
  • A verified date with no row or popup clock is all-day using source-local midnight and next midnight. Date-only end is exclusive; an end clock without a start clock fails. The popup date must still corroborate the row.
  • Identity is ticketweb_{publisherId}_{yyyyMMddTHHmmss} in source-local time. Row order, title edits and UTC DST offsets do not affect it. Different publisher IDs or scheduled occurrences remain distinct. Conflicting popup schedules for the same ID are unsupported and fail rather than guess.
  • Title comes from the row; the joined popup must also have a title, but its display typography may differ (observed plugin replacement-character damage). Identity and schedule, not title text, are authoritative join evidence. Description is sanitized popup text (the plugin may publish only an excerpt). Image is the popup's full-size image when present. Optional description/image gaps are allowed; never fabricate enrichment.
  • SourceUrl is the authoritative same-origin popup title permalink, not #tw-event-dialog-.... The popup's TicketWeb purchase link is separate and is not substituted for that permalink. There is no new normalized ticket-URL field/API change.
  • Published popup venue/address take precedence. An optional verified single-venue configuration fills blanks only for that venue.

docs.title: Failure response
docs.text:
Fetch diagnostics record safe host/path, source/correlation scopes, outcome, retry count and failure category. Monthly join logs report month and count, not payloads or nonce. No adapter-level retries are added; a worker retry re-fetches bootstrap and all months. Stable IDs support normal replay/upsert.

First response: contain repeated work for the affected source; isolate fetch, bootstrap, join, validation or persistence using source/correlation IDs and safe categories; repair and locally validate the full window; then authorize replay through the normal worker. A parse/join failure persists no partial inventory. Suggested alert baselines (not configured by this change): parse success below 90% over 15 minutes/20 fetches; more than five retries per source in ten minutes; sustained dead-letter growth; freshness lag beyond twice the source cadence.

Backend support must be deployed before saving an adapter schema. No OpenAPI generation is needed: this extends source-schema documentation/behavior, not an HTTP DTO.

docs.title: Tockify public calendar adapter
docs.text:
Requires a backend revision registering tockify. Use the canonical public calendar page as the feed URL, e.g. https://calendar.example/sample/, not a fixed-dated API URL or a subscription URL. Generic parsers are unchanged.

{
  "schemaVersion": 3,
  "pipeline": {
    "calendar": {
      "type": "Html",
      "fetch": {
        "method": "GET",
        "requestHeaders": {"User-Agent": "Wheneber/1.0 (+https://app.wheneber.com)"}
      },
      "adapter": {
        "name": "tockify",
        "options": {
          "futureDays": 365,
          "pageSize": 20,
          "maxRequests": 100,
          "maxEvents": 1000,
          "allowedOrigins": ["https://calendar.example"]
        }
      },
      "parser": {}
    },
    "event": {"type": "None", "input": {"mode": "none"}, "parser": {}}
  },
  "validation": {"minEventsPerFetch": 1}
}

docs.title: Inventory, schedule and details
docs.text:
Discovery validates the public bootstrap's calendar name, ID, timezone and canonical URL. The adapter reads the public frontend /api/ngevent pinboard protocol with a rolling startms, start-inclusive=true, showAll=false, and offset increments by actual returned row count. It exhausts metaData.hasNext; neither the bootstrap's first 20 nor a larger guessed max establishes completeness. Page offset drift, duplicate occurrence identities, non-progress, missing metadata and budget overflow fail visibly. Inventory beyond the configured horizon is still enumerated, bounded by the inventory/request caps; only in-window records require detail joins.

Every selected record requires its public detail bootstrap with exactly one matching calendar/occurrence. Detail epoch milliseconds, interpreted using DateTimeOffset.FromUnixTimeMilliseconds, are authoritative, not an ICS schedule or doors clock in prose. A publisher ICS record can differ from its public showtime. Timezone identifiers are checked but never used to reinterpret epoch instants. Zero-duration, all-day and multi-day/range events retain published boundaries. Negative durations, missing dates/timezones and unsupported statuses fail. Published cancelled/canceled/deleted occurrences are excluded. There is no invented default end, date inference or recurrence expansion; already expanded instances use upstream calendar ID plus singleton uid, or repeating uid/rid/tid. The publisher's repeating occurrence token eid.tid is not the mutable when.start.millis; seq is deliberately not an identity component. Repeat detail paths include /rid. Unknown kinds or ambiguous duplicate identities fail rather than adding a current-date/index suffix. Validate real recurring inventory before enabling a new source; rekeying upstream occurrence tokens requires reconciliation, not a claim that IDs survive arbitrary publisher series rewrites.

The output identity excludes sorter, current start, ticket URL and array position. Canonical public detail URLs replace potentially schemeless custom ticket links. Description HTML becomes plain text with scripts/styles/media widgets removed. Images use published absolute HTTP(S) OpenGraph URLs; image URLs are metadata only, never fetched by this adapter. Missing optional description/image/location logs counts, not a whole-run failure. Missing location uses the existing TBD convention.

Optional venue has exactly name, address, evidenceUrl (nonblank, max 500 chars). Use only an independently verified single-venue source fact; evidence must be its same-origin public calendar page. Event where.place/address takes precedence; a different published venue cannot be relabelled. Do not infer an event venue from contact/office chrome or geocode placeholders.

docs.title: Bounds and access
docs.text:
All five options shown are required; unknown keys fail closed. futureDays: 1–730; pageSize: 1–100; maxRequests: 2–1000; maxEvents: 1–5000; allowedOrigins: 1–10 unique default-port HTTPS origins. The shared effective event cap also applies. Every request must match the feed origin and code-owned calendar, detail or exact API query rules. Canonical host changes require operator selection of the new feed, not an automatic host switch. Shared timeout/byte limits, cancellation, restricted header filtering, no cookies/redirects and safe host/path-only fetch logs apply equally to worker and test-fetch.

This is a public read-only frontend protocol, not an authenticated API integration. An indexing robots.txt exclusion is distinct from authentication/access controls. Operators must confirm appropriate publisher use; do not bypass HTTP 401/403, WAF, challenges, private calendars or publisher restrictions. No tokens, cookies, proxy, browser impersonation or alternate-host evasion. The adapter never retries internally.

docs.title: Validation and first response
docs.text:
Compare the entire configured window against an independent inventory (an advertised ICS subscription plus independently decoded public details is useful). Check exact start/end, IDs, images, descriptions, canonical URLs and venue provenance, not only counts. Test-fetch samples omit some detail fields; retain a local full sample. No event list reaches persistence until every required inventory/detail request passes. Freshness is end >= now minus 24 hours; starts at or beyond the future horizon are excluded. A minimum is evaluated through the existing pipeline.

Contain repeated failed runs; isolate discover, inventory, detail_join or quality with SourceId/CorrelationId scopes and shared fetch diagnostics. Recover by correcting configuration/publisher drift, validating locally and test-fetching, then running one separately authorized replay. Existing snapshot IDs make same-ID replay idempotent; migration from old sorter IDs needs explicit reconciliation. Suggested alerts (not automatically provisioned): any required-stage failure or parse success below 99% over 20 runs, >=3 retries/source in 15 minutes, any dead-letter growth, freshness lag >2 scheduled source intervals. Optional-field warning counts are quality signals, not reasons for blind retry.

docs.title: v3 Calendar/Event Type Pair Reference
docs.text: v3 accepts only specific pipeline.calendar.type -> pipeline.event.type combinations.

docs.title: Allowed pairs
docs.text:
• Ics -> None
  • Ics -> Html
  • Ics -> Json
  • Html -> Html
  • Html -> Json
  • Html -> None only with an allowlisted code-owned calendar adapter (eventon, ticketweb, ticketmaster, tockify, or journey)
  • Json -> None
  • Json -> Html
  • Json -> Json
  • Rss -> None
  • Rss -> Html
  • Rss -> Json

Any pair outside this list fails schema admission.

docs.title: Important implications
docs.text:
• Html -> None is rejected for normal parser execution. Code-owned complete projection adapters require this pair; their calendar/event parsers must be empty and no separate detail stage is permitted.
  • Ics -> None and Rss -> None remain valid when calendar stage already contains needed fields.
  • Json -> None is valid when calendar payload already includes full event fields.

docs.title: Recommendation
docs.text:
Choose the simplest allowed pair that still gives complete and accurate event data.

  • If detail fetch is unnecessary and your type supports -> None, use it.
  • If detail fetch is needed, use -> Html or -> Json with conservative fetch limits.
